entries.title: Scheduled workflows and shared Flower work
entries.summary: Automation owns definitions, context and artifacts; ReDevPlugin owns durable scheduling and published agent.work. Canonical Floret owns admission, execution, approval and observation, with no second model runtime. Tessiven business linkage is deferred.

entries.title: Product storage placement and lifecycle
entries.summary: Redeven allocates feature roots; published upstream owners retain opaque formats. Storage inspection reports bounded observations, never deletion authority or backup success. Environment data, Desktop profiles and external projects have separate ownership; relocation requires an explicit offline operation with verified recovery state.

entries.title: Host application keyboard, pointer and composition
entries.summary: Published Floe controllers own keyboard, composition and pointer gestures; product adapters bind them to painted window generations. Both motion paths use the same target authority, microtask coalescing, explicit flush and cancellation; platform bindings must not install another raw-event listener.

entries.title: Host application viewing, display and resource lifetime
entries.summary: Runtime/native events own application facts; bootstrap and published SDK own viewing, geometry and immutable resources. Modes Automatic/Clarity first/Motion first/Save data persist through reload; same selection,locale/theme never reconnect. [Performance](../operations/host-application-performance.md) owns budgets.

entries.title: Managed service release discovery and version selection
entries.summary: Registries provide release candidates; Manager validates immutable identity, compatibility and reviewed update plans. Schema-v2 `ReleaseCandidate` carries source/version/time/channel, trust, compatibility, immutable identity, verification/selectability and installed relation. Verification cannot reorder visible rows. Cancellation changes no state; failed checks retain stale last success without blocking actions or toasts.

entries.title: Managed service template publication, acquisition and formats
entries.summary: Published templates own definitions, formats and passive resources; Redeven validates offline bundles and authorizes imported original directories. Strict decode,consecutive in-memory transformations,current validation/passive-resource checks feed one executor.

entries.title: Service template marketplace discovery and acquisition
entries.summary: The market discovers passive evidence. Deployment requires exact originals acquired through Desktop or Runtime.

entries.title: Personal service templates and pinned source derivation
entries.summary: Personal service templates combine an independently editable product definition with verified immutable upstream files. They preserve source provenance without mutating the source library or existing instances.

entries.title: Service management recovery and resource ownership
entries.summary: Registry owns transactions, allocations and identities; fresh backend facts govern recovery and deletion. Unknown ownership is shown honestly. Frontend code never substitutes Retry or Restart for unavailable Start. A failed Host maintenance hook may be bypassed only through an administrator's reviewed plan, and only for verified resources.

entries.title: Web service browser routing and authorization
entries.summary: Registry access mode selects protected unified proxy or Desktop loopback; current Environment/forward authority governs every handoff. Backend normalization accepts `3000`, `:3000` and absolute/scheme-less HTTP(S) with exact `localhost`, numeric `127.0.0.0/8` or `::1`. Renderer checks are feedback only.

entries.title: Independent Web Environment Center
entries.summary: Desktop combines an environment center with its existing local Runtime lifecycle. Web Center has one administrator, with no registration, users, roles, organizations or user ACL service. Labels/hostnames grant no trust. Revisions/sequences fence observations; late completion cannot navigate canceled pending tabs or cancel open route owners.

entries.title: Flower startup and recovery presentation
entries.summary: Both carriers project one readiness owner and typed Stop/Retry, retaining drafts/navigation. Close failure needs restart; contradictory facts are nonretryable. Activity, Workbench and Settings share readiness. After Runtime readiness, retain Flower loading until the first authoritative list page or selected detail is applied. Confirmed empty lists admit; empty partial-ready envelopes do not. Remaining pages load progressively. Embedded conversations wait only for their own detail.

entries.title: Tessiven immutable canvases, DSL and display compatibility
entries.summary: Runtime owns immutable canvas YAML and contiguous version migration; clients render a frozen data-only display contract. The `tessiven_canvas_library` SQLite lineage starts at schema v1. Paths must be unique, acyclic and complete, with source validation, target validation and semantic checks.

entries.title: Native Runtime bridge
entries.summary: native-bridge --state-root attaches only to existing Runtime via owner socket. Stdio uses redeven-native-runtime-h2/1 and native-runtime CONNECT. Missing/stopped/incompatible targets fail without install/start/address fallback/Desktop credentials; disconnect releases client only.

entries.title: Flower browser source ownership
entries.summary: Runtime authorizes targets; source Host owns CDP/extension adapters. Each page has one debugger/input order; opener ancestry stays private. Source loss retires affected bindings only; unknown effects never replay or create replacement authority. Runtime discovers supported Chrome and Chromium installations by opaque installation ID.

entries.title: Flower browser Linux preparation
entries.summary: Runtime discovers installs/registers Native Messaging; Host Applications owns graphical lifecycle. Clients pass opaque IDs. Personal profiles remain; missing/unsafe/unsupported sources fail before launch. The authenticated `POST /_redeven_proxy/api/browser/extension/remote` action requires read, write and execute authority.

entries.title: Database schema migration ownership
entries.summary: Each repository migrates its own opaque stores. Validate full SQLite/WAL before readiness; contiguous atomic edges preserve records. Future, drifted, wrong-kind or unsupported state remains untouched. Failure blocks only its service without upstream repair or database replacement.

entries.title: AI readiness and service generation lifecycle
entries.summary: One process-local Redeven controller owns AI construction/retry/publication/leases/drain/close; Floret owns durable facts. Non-AI surfaces stay usable. Startup recovers unfinished replacements, opens the Floret owner with bounded waiting, migrates product data, activates and publishes. Floret's worker prepares historical threads.

entries.title: Runtime startup presentation
entries.summary: `redeven run` startup is modeled as a lifecycle event stream. Human terminal output and public machine events are renderers over the same state snapshot, while a separate private Desktop report carries machine-only attach data and stable failure codes needed to open or recover the local Env App safely.

entries.title: Observation and target action events
entries.summary: Target actions are ordinary Flower tool observations. An action publishes running, result, and error observations with tool ID, target ID, execution location, approval state, action summary, and attachment descriptor. The UI reads these events through the existing stream and resolves screenshots through the canonical attachment preview path.

entries.title: Local UI surface
entries.summary: Local UI supports independent concurrent Desktop/browser sessions. Versioned SQLite owns one-shot authorization/spend; network policy owns exposure/password/certificates/migrations. Local UI bind parsing accepts `localhost`, canonical loopback IP literals, concrete non-loopback unicast IPv4 and IPv6 literals, and the `0.0.0.0` and `::` wildcards.

entries.title: Env App session event transport
entries.summary: One Floe HTTP proxy runtime serves each Env App session and all built-in/plugin logical event streams. Features cannot consume parallel native HTTP/1.1 slots, retarget upstream identity or create another transport. Session multiplexing removes those event requests from the browser HTTP pool; changing request priority alone cannot do so.

entries.title: Web Services interface
entries.summary: Activity/Workbench share service list/drawer: identity, state, action, facts. Template previews show source, version, access mode and disk requirements. A closed keyboard disclosure retains technical identity/endpoints/lifecycle/paths; commands and installation steps are never expanded by default.

entries.title: Human remote desktop sessions
entries.summary: Redeven owns authorization/sessions/placement/audit; Floe Native Apps owns OS capture/input/codecs/playback and Linux acquisition/service. Share signed-in desktop without private replacement or policy changes. Disconnect preserves work; unavailable media revokes input until fresh frame.

entries.title: Administrator-authorized remote desktop deployment over SSH
entries.summary: Desktop owns SSH authorization/UI lifetime, Floe Native Apps privileged preparation and Runtime service authorization/audit. Only the owning root/main frame of an RWX-authorized SSH environment uses typed deployment IPC. Sensitive admin streams retain no stdout/stderr diagnostics.

entries.title: Persistent remote desktop sharing approval
entries.summary: Redeven owns sharing preference/reset; Floe Native Apps owns OS consent/private recovery. This user Portal path is separate from SSH system-service deployment. [Feature access](host-applications.md#feature-access) is independent of OS consent and approval reuse. Pause/remove revokes desktop sessions and fences admission without changing application access or shared grants. Remove clears Redeven desktop preferences; later capability reads cannot reenable it.

entries.title: Remote desktop connection launcher
entries.summary: Host Applications separates connection, setup and feature management. Access settings directly manages independent application-window and desktop access. Local application launch needs no remote-access permission. Setup asks only for missing grants; daily connection stays focused.

entries.title: Flowersec transport for graphical windows
entries.summary: Flowersec owns encrypted multiplexed transport/backpressure; Redeven resources/authorization/routes. Env App resource-management requests, including the forward touch immediately before opening a graphical window, use its active Flowersec session HTTP carrier.

entries.title: Remote desktop viewer interaction
entries.summary: Published input/playback and session contracts own current-frame authority. Recovery keeps controls usable; disconnect stops media/input with confirmed removal or Retry. Frozen pixels never imply connection. This desktop-only policy does not apply to host application windows, which use their own upstream cursor contract.

entries.title: Remote desktop media and input scheduling
entries.summary: Published native packages own capture/encode/playback; session contract owns authority/generations. Physical-seat capture uses one latest-sample mailbox and separate 60Hz cursor stream. An authenticated inherited descriptor attaches media; bounded backpressure retires attachment instead of blocking input release. Encoder reset begins a new keyframe chain without discarding transported references.

entries.title: Host application catalog, platforms and preparation
entries.summary: Redeven authorizes catalog, instances and independent shares; published native libraries own platform execution and preparation. Host Applications is available in Activity navigation and the Workbench launcher. Full-permission `PUT /_redeven_proxy/api/{host-applications,remote-desktop}/access` requires an explicit state.

entries.title: Host application lifecycle and Linux instance recovery
entries.summary: Viewing, sharing, closing windows and ending processes remain distinct across platforms. The first Force quit action only enters that state; only its final confirmation sends the destructive host request. Instance records bind opaque ID, authorized owner, metadata, boot/PID/start, component identity and private backend endpoint. Reusable window IDs never grant authority.

entries.title: macOS application authority, capture and lifecycle
entries.summary: Runtime opens installed macOS bundles as its user and binds capture/input to actual process/window generations. Remote input shares the real foreground session: activate/raise the bound window and verify foreground, focused AX window and pointer ownership before injection.

entries.title: Portable native Runtime binaries
entries.summary: Shared builder owns Runtime/Gateway terminal linkage: Linux runs on glibc/musl without host loader; Darwin requires matching Apple build. Every shipped Redeven Runtime enables terminal-go's `floeterm_native` build tag with cgo. Cross builds select the explicit `<arch>-linux-gnu` or `<arch>-unknown-linux-gnu` compiler pair; preflight fails before source copying or asset generation when the compiler or static libraries are missing.

entries.title: Managed Web Service opening
entries.summary: Templates parse entrances; Runtime verifies/persists preparation; Desktop navigates and Env App presents. HTTP401 proves availability only; failures offer recovery and never stop healthy apps. Missing or rotated output and an absent verified record require an explicitly chosen restart to produce a new entrance.

entries.title: Independent Host service lifecycle
entries.summary: Apps own execution; Redeven owns authorized lifecycle/native identity/launch records/opening. Restart preserves PID/generation. Distinguish absent/mismatched/uninspectable: only absence permits launch; opening failure never stops app. This is not a resident service supervisor or another binary.

entries.title: Managed Web Services
entries.summary: Redeven owns instances/resources/bindings/operations/forwards; verified templates define behavior. Load published redeven-service-templates before Registry/Manager. Recommendations default new installs; explicit compatible releases override and later catalogs never change installed identity. Failed creation removes only verified new containers, preserving data/workspace for review.

entries.title: Managed Service operation progress
entries.summary: Manager Reporter owns live output; Registry owns history. Capture/storage/transport failures must not expose secrets, queries, private paths or control bytes. Explicit rejection offers fresh review with non-secret inputs; secrets clear with the drawer. Ambiguous transport outcomes offer read-only request-ID receipt lookup, never blind POST replay.

entries.title: Managed Service Instance Configuration
entries.summary: Verified template owns baseline; Redeven owns overrides, release/digest, resources, secrets and rebuilds. One resolver combines baseline/differences. Apply requires stopped state, current revision/plan/risk checks; failure preserves prior state or explicitly reports rollback failure.

entries.title: Runtime Service snapshot
entries.summary: Typed Runtime snapshots expose protocol/version, compatibility epoch, capabilities, readiness and workload identity to Desktop/Local UI. Runtime publishes its own service protocol and independent component version. Desktop manages Runtime lifecycle through its verified target-host connection, placement bridge and lifecycle coordinator.

entries.title: Runtime session permission gates
entries.summary: Runtime validates session metadata and supported app/channel pairs before intersecting control-plane and local policy. Read permits existing monitor/process observations; process termination independently requires execute and cannot inherit authority from visibility.

entries.title: Runtime system monitoring
entries.summary: Monitor owns one CPU/memory/network/process snapshot for page and Workbench. All OS-marked loopback interfaces are excluded from the shared network counters/rates. Failed network samples never enter history or fall back to unfiltered totals; later samples recover independently while other metrics remain usable.

entries.title: Runtime transport composition and Env App recovery
entries.summary: Published Flowersec owns acquisition, framing, retries and connection replacement; Redeven maps exact product authorization onto one current Env App session. Published Flowersec owns Transportv3 connection/session/RPC/streams; Floeterm owns terminal lifecycle.

entries.title: Runtime artifact spend and control pool
entries.summary: Opaque single-spend control/data artifacts bind each Lease to a digest-global tombstone. Persist idempotent bootstrap/top-up identities; reject stale, duplicate, malformed, expired or cross-environment responses. Replenishment/relink are explicit terminal transitions, never silent fallback.

entries.title: Runtime terminal lifecycle
entries.summary: Floeterm owns PTY/Ghostty VT, geometry/controller epoch, input encoding, history/reset and atomic Presentation. `/_redeven_proxy/api/terminal/history-retention` is the product settings adapter: GET reads defaults or an authorized session; admin-only PUT persists and activates defaults; POST applies explicit limits to a session using its connection ID and transport generation.

entries.title: Product RPC request encoding
entries.summary: Redeven codecs construct JSON; Flowersec validates/dispatches. File creation preserves empty content and omitted encoding; absent options stay omitted, explicit false/empty retain meaning. Invalid input fails before dispatch and needs codec repair, not retries or weaker validation.

entries.title: Git workspace inventory lifecycle
entries.summary: Git queries expose bounded immutable snapshots with revision-bound paging. Git/Files mutations coordinate topology and invalidate snapshots around effects; display grants no authority. Oversized/stale/malformed/exhausted reads return bounded typed errors without losing Flowersec session.

entries.title: Env App upstream web dependencies
entries.summary: Env App adapts published Floe UI/runtime/protocol, FloeBrowser projection, Floeterm terminal-web and Flowersec helpers. Pins: Floe Boot/Core/Protocol v0.101.15, FloeBrowser v0.1.28, Floeterm terminal-web v0.20.0, Flowersec Core v5.12.0. Floeterm supplies Presentation/session exports.

entries.title: Env App terminal and surface composition
entries.summary: Env App adapts Floeterm PTY facts and Floe shell, focus, selection and KeepAlive. File preview defaults to main surface. A session owns <=one view. Selecting it activates/focuses that view, even from standalone/another view; unowned sessions appear alone.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin host integration boundary
entries.summary: Redeven consumes one coordinated published ReDevPlugin Go/npm/Rust/machine release. Product adapters never recreate upstream runtime, permission or storage mechanics. Failed channel binding grants nothing and cannot close the host channel; request panic releases admission and HTTP contains failure.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin Redeven adapters
entries.summary: Redeven binds authenticated sessions, source policy, business capabilities and placement to released ReDevPlugin. Market owns default transport;integration closes caller-owned package transport on failure/shutdown. Connector transports independently follow upstream pool lifecycle.

entries.title: Plugin platform integration
entries.summary: Redeven mounts one released ReDevPlugin Host/HTTP namespace/client/scope. Unproven identity fails closed. Mount one released Host/HTTP namespace/client/scope at an explicit root. Session close uses released durable four-hash drain;remove authentication after exact acknowledgement.

entries.title: Plugin process sessions
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin Process Broker owns processes; Redeven supplies authenticated scope/permission/minimal environment/secrets/state/audit. Opaque handles expose bounded binary stdio, no second protocol. Overflow may lose output; close/disable/uninstall/revoke/owner teardown stops owned work.

entries.title: Plugin background entries
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns headless Worker lifecycle and durable intervals. A plugin may declare runtime_start, on_demand or interval. The first two use the platform background manager: starts are idempotent, scoped to the installed instance and environment, and independent of visible Activity or Workbench surfaces.

entries.title: Plugin package and runtime lifecycle
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns package inspection, installation, source identity, durable receipts, runtime readiness and retained data. The Host validates ordinary package structure, hashes, manifest, capability contracts and source policy. Plugin signatures, publisher trust, signed release references, and official-only admission do not participate.

entries.title: Plugin surface recovery and permissions
entries.summary: Env App owns one authenticated plugin client, shared scope and installation observer. Panel closure/reconnect retains exact request identity and outcome; refresh never becomes another mutation or lifecycle. First terminal surface error refreshes owner inventory once,never execution/same-revision auto-retry.

entries.title: Plugin market consumption
entries.summary: Redeven consumes one complete public market representation. Official and community are display classifications, not admission privileges. Packages remain ordinary `.redevplugin` assets in GitHub Releases; every installation uses the released Host inspection and durable installation APIs.

entries.title: Container execution and operation observation
entries.summary: Container operations bind exact engine/endpoint/resource. Public terminal taxonomy distinguishes storage, registry availability, rate limit, missing and denied; UI maps known codes to localized guidance with durable timeline.

entries.title: Container resource capability, console and usage facts
entries.summary: Native resource services own endpoint-bound execution, admission and reconciliation; the console presents typed authorized facts and drafts. Disk usage never authorizes cleanup or overrides the reference preflight. [Runtime execution](containers-operation-observation.md#engine-execution) owns discovery, endpoint binding, typed CLI reads and normalization; [volume usage](#volume-observations) owns reference completeness and independent usage reads.

entries.title: Container engine service management
entries.summary: One ContainerServiceController owns Docker/Podman discovery, lifecycle, configuration, preflight identity and reconciliation. Known management/health faults retain ID/implementation/config sources/actions. Missing CLI/permission/timeout/unknown is not stopped.

entries.title: Single-administrator Web Center access
entries.summary: Center has one administrator and multiple devices. Unix socket checks service UID/root, never SSH/tunnel/loopback/header claims. recover fences business and authorizes setup; recover --offline --origin needs stopped exclusive state. Exclusive lock protects AES-GCM SQLite. center.key pins instance/origin/initialization; missing/corrupt committed state fails.

entries.title: Runtime access sessions
entries.summary: Runtime accessgate alone owns validity/revocation. EnvAppShell binds remote access readiness to the exact connected client after access.status/access.resume succeeds. Each replacement channel must confirm access independently; late success or failure from a retired channel cannot authorize or disconnect its replacement.

entries.title: Runtime two-factor authentication
entries.summary: Runtime accessgate independently requires password then TOTP/recovery for browser/direct/Cloud sessions. These commands do not alter SSH keys, sshd policy, PAM, host passwords, or execution identity. Authentication state and secrets are not diagnostic export inputs.

entries.title: Local UI exposure, HTTPS identity and explicit certificate changes
entries.summary: Runtime owns public listeners, saved HTTPS identity and admission; Desktop presents explicit next-start settings. Signing failure retains only addresses covered by the prior valid leaf, reports certificate_refresh_failed and retries recovery.

entries.title: Permission policy and filesystem scope
entries.summary: Runtime policy is authoritative even after control-plane session authorization. Repository-rule discovery, structured file reads and delivered-file reads use Registry.OpenRead. It resolves current policy, rechecks the selected root, walks canonical components through pinned os.Root handles, rejects substituted symlinks and compares opened identities before returning a descriptor.

entries.title: Plugin platform integration security
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin accepts authenticated host identity and source policy, never browser-claimed trust. Resolve only stored channel metadata with exact nonempty channel/user/environment identities. Cache by owner-session hash; all four hashes must match. Canonical HTTP route: /_redevplugin/api/plugins.

entries.title: Verified Environment access routes
entries.summary: Desktop associates Gateway routes only through trusted attachment ID, Runtime public ID and Gateway-key matches; health is independent. Names/URLs/renderer claims grant nothing. Local/Cloud ownership stays separate; missing/unverified routes require explicit replacement.

entries.title: Host application component cache
entries.summary: Published artifactcache owns verification, locking and eviction. Desktop supplies its private directory, seven-day idle retention and 2 GB budget plus document-local transfers/UI. Unknown catalogs fail and cleanup cannot negate successful preparation.

entries.title: Desktop qualification lifecycle
entries.summary: Desktop supervisor owns scenario/resource/cleanup deadlines. Acceptance leaves no owned processes, bridges or fixtures; preserve production Quit and independent Runtime. Names/ports grant no stop authority. Timeout/interruption/forced cleanup/residue fails with retained manifest evidence.

entries.title: Desktop development sessions and bundles
entries.summary: Launcher owns source-bound Desktop/Runtime/Gateway bundles and checkout-stable profile; shared build tooling owns dependency preparation.

entries.title: Desktop Web Service browser window
entries.summary: Desktop owns protected target views, toolbar, navigation and cleanup over Runtime-authorized Web Service routes. Invalid navigation rejects, while marked upstream failure offers local retry without reauthorizing or restarting the app. When the trusted Desktop Shell bridge is present, Env App requests a semantic Web Service window instead of creating a renderer popup.

entries.title: Desktop host application titlebar
entries.summary: Redeven owns the compact host toolbar; macOS capture/Xpra own commands and sessions, Desktop supplies native geometry. It never sends server shutdown or force-kills the application. macOS quit retains its existing application-wide confirmation. The control is unavailable until its selected target has decoded pixels.

entries.title: Desktop shell theme state
entries.summary: One validated Desktop theme snapshot drives Welcome, Env App, chrome and generated documents. Selection paints before persistence, retaining acknowledged state, drafts/focus/content and Retry on failure. Admit ids/defaults/metadata from published Floe `/themes`; never copy palettes or weaken forced-color/high-contrast behavior. OS changes apply only in system mode.

entries.title: Environment library, registrations and card presentation
entries.summary: Welcome projects registration owners into stable Environment cards. Title/description/search/refresh/create lead; categories carry counts, cards Runtime/window state. Snapshot errors appear only when present, without empty reserved rows.

entries.title: Desktop interaction continuity
entries.summary: Welcome owns interaction sessions; Launcher/Runtime own business operations. Before the first asynchronous submission, one synchronous transition records the attempt, closes its menu and opens its operation surface. The interaction-continuity package command runs required state and real component suites, including the production snapshot subscription and observer.

entries.title: Desktop Welcome navigation
entries.summary: Welcome navigation is local and immediate, independent of IPC/Runtime preparation. Each popup has one published Floe presence owner. Closing immediately revokes input/accessibility, freezes placement and retains DOM through exit.

entries.title: Desktop transport recovery and model-source sessions
entries.summary: A placement bridge owns one immutable recovery generation and exact Environment session. The existing coordinator waits for Desktop transport readiness inside published source acquisition instead of racing another connection controller. A ready bridge plus repeated retryable upper-layer transport failures requests bounded SSH verification once per protocol attempt; it neither restarts Runtime nor replays requests.

entries.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations
entries.summary: Desktop uses saved SSH connection/placement for host/container Runtime. Omitted password reuses exact private scope; changes fail during leases and never cross scopes. Explicit passwordless opens try configured keys/agent in batch mode even for password registrations; passive observations may defer.

entries.title: Desktop WSL runtime operations
entries.summary: Windows11x64 runs Electron, not native Local/container Runtime. Register initialized Linux x64 WSL2 targets; manage only exact distro/user Runtime. Missing/old/uninitialized targets or broken commands/packages/Bridge need visible explicit recovery. UI recovery copy may show Microsoft WSL commands for the user to run.

entries.title: Environment settings sessions, connections and presentation
entries.summary: One target-bound settings session owns connection/access drafts and immediate opening. Local opens Access & security without a connection editor. Access management uses existing WSL authority only after exact-distribution discovery confirms it is running; opening/loading never starts stopped distros. Distinguish current password constraints from saved next-start configuration.

entries.title: Desktop SSH environment settings
entries.summary: SSH creation/editing share one form and registration API. Common controls precede advanced options, retained in an inspectable summary. Failures preserve drafts. Registration contracts own connections/secrets, while Environment settings owns the window, tab, draft and asynchronous recovery lifetime.

entries.title: Desktop Runtime coordination and readiness
entries.summary: One target-bound coordinator admits managed Local, WSL, SSH and container lifecycle work. The current binary supplies temporary exact inventory and best-effort stop. Builds, downloads, archive preparation, upload and extraction belong to package progress, never process discovery.

entries.title: Desktop managed Environment reinstall
entries.summary: Wipe reinstall confirms exact target/root, verifies package, attempts stop, replaces root, verifies startup and cleans old data. Unknown process or broken state cannot block filesystem recovery. Both modes are named Reinstall. [Interaction continuity](desktop-interaction-continuity.md) owns confirmation sessions; timeout/cancellation preserve journal and diagnostics.

entries.title: Desktop application updates
entries.summary: One Desktop update coordinator serves every entry. Unsupported, development or misplaced builds offer manual recovery. Serialize `idle`, `checking`, `available`, `downloading`, `ready`, `installing`, `blocked` and `error` transitions. Repeated checks reuse the operation; never start a second download.

entries.title: CodeSpace system-browser access
entries.summary: Desktop resolves trusted resource identity over Environment transport into short-lived loopback entry. The system browser never receives a private Local UI `/cs/<id>` URL, an environment credential, or a raw gateway header. Runtime accepts only this shaped loopback origin or the built-in numeric-loopback origin as presentation metadata; that metadata never selects an upstream dial target.

entries.title: Native Desktop CodeSpace access
entries.summary: Desktop owns CodeSpace window/profile/loopback listener/route; Runtime owns editor generation/permissions/AccessGate. Only the trusted environment root submits `loading`/`open` with a DNS-safe CodeSpace ID. [Window status surfaces](../ui/window-status-surfaces.md) owns presentation.

entries.title: Optional Runtime Cloud egress
entries.summary: Cloud is optional Runtime functionality. Route operations retain an operation ID, expected revisions, target fingerprint, confirmation and queryable result. Changing an attachment, certificate, route or Cloud identity invalidates previous consent. An unknown result queries the original operation.

entries.title: Gateway device trust and host operations
entries.summary: Paired devices receive independent Gateway access, never accounts, roles or host-management grants. Verify HTTPS using only that CA, then signed Gateway identity before persisting device trust. Never disable TLS or install global CAs. Packages expire after ten minutes; consumption admits no second device.

entries.title: Independent Gateway service
entries.summary: Gateway independently owns attachment/device admission/relay without Cloud account, cached authority or public Internet. Cloud alone owns membership/organizations/roles. Gateway has no Cloud machine/Namespace/renewal/delegated-publication/command ownership.

entries.title: Gateway network settings
entries.summary: Verified host admin atomically saves share endpoints/listeners/Host restrictions. Desktop Settings shows the saved listener bindings separately from active addresses. A pending restart exposes an explicit review action using the same Gateway lifecycle confirmation and progress as card maintenance.

entries.title: Gateway Desktop interactions
entries.summary: Desktop enrolls Local, SSH, WSL and container Runtimes through one app session. Padded Dropdown selector/trailing Cancel opens fixed wizard;empty inventory offers recovery and wrapped/touch content retains height. Creation offers Not now/Add Gateway access.

entries.title: Gateway access sessions
entries.summary: Desktop reaches joined Runtime over its outbound Flowersec Gateway connection; Gateway forwards to fixed application entry without dialing a Runtime URL. Entry expiry never shortens established sessions. Revoking a client closes its live streams and fences its pending artifacts.

entries.title: Independent Gateway qualification
entries.summary: Independent Gateway acceptance uses production handlers, host placements, real application authentication and multilingual management. Evidence qualifies only exercised device admission and revocation paths. UI/process qualification stays separate from exact-main push gates and release packaging.

entries.title: Browser Editor runtime
entries.summary: Code App owns Browser Editor runtime. Local UI `/cs/<id>/` and remote `cs-*` hosts open codespaces; Desktop/Env App use workspace-engine APIs to prepare/update versions.

entries.title: File preview rendering, formats and viewport
entries.summary: Redeven owns source/authority/modes; released renderers own parsing/layout. Existing More or compact headerless trigger opens a bounded absolute overlay without viewport movement. Menu/keyboard/content share owner and restore origin focus; no dedicated row/header icon.

entries.title: File preview actions and dismissal
entries.summary: Redeven owns file actions, drafts and immediate cancellation; Floe owns titlebar, tabs and exit presence. Sorting moves opaque tabs/neighbors without external borders or insertion bars; release commits, cancel restores, reduced motion skips settling.

entries.title: Flower companion presence, composer and motion
entries.summary: Collapsed Flower projects canonical work and connection-local editor intent through one retained textarea. Priority decides whether to show a decision, draft, status target or inspection. Shared shell motion preserves draft, selection, IME and focus; historical completion never becomes new feedback.

entries.title: Flower conversation selection and detail reads
entries.summary: Acknowledge navigation before transcript work. One loader owns select/reselect/reconnect/retry; position transcript/active sequence before reveal. Restored labels/groups/turns are static; folded turns cannot block readiness and manual folds retain labels.

entries.title: Activity navigation restoration
entries.summary: One Redeven Activity record selects the saved target before mounting and commits navigation/recency immediately. Legacy dynamic IDs remain pending until the current plugin directory can validate and migrate their stable target. Loading and cache authority follow [Env App resource snapshots](env-resource-cache.md).

entries.title: Env App resource snapshots
entries.summary: Floe owns disposable cache restoration/coalescing/fencing/persistence/eviction; Redeven verifies identity/projection. Resource lists retain successful data while refresh animates only its icon. Cache grants nothing; denial clears, connectivity failure retains facts with Retry.

entries.title: Page loading, asynchronous feedback and document recovery
entries.summary: Initial loads occupy final geometry. Refresh retains successful same-resource content, including empty results, with stable item DOM/focus/expansion/scroll. Pagination feedback stays at the end.

entries.title: Whole-window status surfaces
entries.summary: Floe owns window layout/retry/artwork; Redeven maps actual access/connection state. The document never receives Runtime credentials or user draft contents. Status styling is never injected into third-party application documents. Published shimmer supports reduced motion and forced colors; long translated copy and technical details must remain readable without horizontal scrolling.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas navigation, relationships and Flower reading
entries.summary: Published Floe owns graph layout/routing/paint; Tessiven supplies canonical topology and details. Browser popup and native opening failures remain visible; never silently choose another route.

entries.title: Runtime settings
entries.summary: Env owns destinations/drafts/adapters; Floe owns layout/navigation/modal presence/focus. Retain work surfaces and usable narrow controls.

entries.title: Flower extensions
entries.summary: Shared Flower retains Skills/MCP/Plugins management through typed authenticated carrier adapters. MCP edits HTTP endpoints or local executable/one-argument-per-line. Never prefill secrets: omission preserves, explicit empty object clears. Retain search/enabled filter/tools/checks/confirmed removal.

entries.title: UI presentation transactions
entries.summary: Navigation selects synchronously, paints intent, commits target visibility, then focuses/resizes/scrolls/measures after content paint. Floe owns visual/committed value separation; Redeven applies it across heavy product surfaces without duplicating business state.

entries.title: Env App floating layer order
entries.summary: Env App assigns global bands for windows, Flower, plugins, modals and commands; interaction reorders only its band. Upstream elastic dragging resists boundary overflow, retains a reachable header and returns the window inside safe bounds on release/interruption.

entries.title: Dialog content placement
entries.summary: Published Floe owns Dialog structure; Redeven supplies localized content/actions. Floe Webapp 0.84.0 removes the ambiguous `description` parameter from `Dialog` and `ConfirmDialog`. Global dialogs and drawers reserve the visible application header before allocating their body height.

entries.title: Adaptive desktop and mobile navigation
entries.summary: Desktop and mobile remain distinct interaction modes; narrow desktop regions use temporary drawers without rewriting saved placement. Files/Git navigation begins with its mode switch, without a separate Files title row or reserved header space. The switch uses the published field height, including its border and padding, so the sidebar and single-row file toolbar dividers align at every interface scale.

entries.title: Git workspace generations, diffs and visual state
entries.summary: Exact client capabilities and monotonic generations fence Git inventory/diffs/filesystem decoration. Retain shell/navigation with panel-local loading/errors; Files navigation never waits for Git. Nested file references and effects use JSON-only transport.

entries.title: Shared surface material
entries.summary: Published Floe owns material and motion. Both first-party renderers set `theme.defaultSurfaceStyle: soft-neumorphic`; [published dependencies](../architecture/env-app-upstream-web-dependencies.md) own versions/registry requirements. Use released Button/Card/selection/progress/Dialog/FloatingWindow treatments; hover preserves selected fill/text.

entries.title: Product accessibility for AI agents
entries.summary: Redeven owns accessible names/state/relationships while preserving layout, handlers, focus and inert exclusion. Scope claims accurately: accessibility edits alone certify neither WCAG nor model performance. Select uses combobox/listbox/option semantics; Dropdown remains an action menu.

entries.title: Input focus boundaries
entries.summary: Published Floe owns focus presentation; Redeven supplies layout, semantic state and explicit compound-input boundaries. Buttons, links, checkboxes, and switches retain their distinct keyboard focus indicators; buttons inside an input boundary follow the upstream compound-control treatment.

entries.title: Workbench composition, input and surface lifetime
entries.summary: Published Floe owns canvas composition and generic input mechanics; Redeven supplies permission, persistence and selected-widget adapters. Pristine runtimes receive one English welcome canvas: two editable notes beside Files, Terminal and Monitoring in three unnamed regions.

entries.title: Workbench terminal interaction
entries.summary: Floeterm terminal-go owns PTY, VT, geometry, controller epoch, semantic history and atomic Presentation. terminal-web renders one canvas/view and collects local input. [Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md#companion) owns its measured footer; Workbench supplies none.

entries.title: Terminal fonts across client devices
entries.summary: Env App owns document-local terminal fonts. New preferences use bundled JetBrains Mono at size 12; existing IDs/sizes remain unchanged and each client resolves availability. The menu separates bundled fonts from available local fonts and exposes the saved selection through accessible pressed state; an unavailable saved selection remains visible but cannot be newly selected.

entries.title: Terminal session groups
entries.summary: Runtime catalogs own groups, assignments and named views; Activity/Workbench share environment projection with local expansion/active view. View thumbnail opens layout picker, name activates; footer targets active view, row picker may change inactive view.2–32 slot choices preserve members/vacancies/selection.

entries.title: Plugin package review, installation and saved-data recovery
entries.summary: All plugin sources share released package inspection, exact review and durable installation. Market installs automatically inspect the selected repository/release/asset and expected package/security/contract hashes. Direct installation accepts HTTPS, GitHub repository or uploaded `.redevplugin` bytes.

entries.title: File icon presentation
entries.summary: Floe owns filename recognition, SVG icons and palettes; Redeven supplies names, directory/link metadata and size. Formats retain reviewed distinctions and unknown files use the generic upstream icon. Icons confer no preview/execution/extraction authority, whose independent format and permission checks remain.

entries.title: Files context menus
entries.summary: Floe owns file-menu placement, scrolling, gestures and dismissal; Redeven supplies bounds/actions/locales. Keep menus eight CSS pixels inside Files/surface/visible viewport intersection. Invalid bounds close; never escape global layers or duplicate Workbench transforms.

entries.title: Plugin Center interaction
entries.summary: Redeven owns retained Center navigation/search/filter/selection/scroll; Floe owns dialogs/presence/input. Authoring starts with centered composer and quiet canvas.

entries.title: Plugin discovery, placement and layout continuity
entries.summary: Redeven owns navigation/pins/geometry; published ReDevPlugin owns slots/authority. Tiles launch once without pin overlays. ContextMenu/right-click/Shift+F10 exposes info and current-mode pins; pinning keeps Launcher open and dismissal restores focus.

entries.title: Flower turn submission, outbox and input recall
entries.summary: One immutable transport outbox captures ordinary submitted text and resources before asynchronous admission. Product admission uses published SendAck and narrow canonical summaries. HTTP and RPC return admission identity without a post-commit history read; authorized window observation supplies presentation separately.

entries.title: Flower references, origin context and canonical admission
entries.summary: Connection-local file/directory/page/thread chips retain ordered IDs/labels in memory until explicit Send. [Tool runtime](../ai/ai-tool-runtime.md#runtime) owns one-pass canonical MessageReference/context admission.

entries.title: Absolute filesystem directory selection
entries.summary: Floe owns picker navigation/validity/request lifetime; Redeven supplies authoritative path context/connection/locales/form. Existing browse/cache owner shows only visited target's snapshot while verifying. Uncached targets preserve readable listing with separate pending intent.

entries.title: Personal directory favorites
entries.summary: Runtime stores independent ordered favorites/revisions per authenticated namespace/endpoint/user. Files composes Home, Computer and favorites into one Quick access list, deduplicated by absolute path with authoritative root labels and permissions preserved.

entries.title: Flower working directory navigation
entries.summary: Flower owns draft/thread directory intent; Env App destination navigation. The [conversation sidebar](flower-thread-sidebar.md#directory-view) can start a new draft from a listed directory. Conversation transcript and thread-list menus expose browsing, opening a terminal, and copying the working directory.

entries.title: Flower Activity companion and contextual Ask Flower placement
entries.summary: One retained Flower surface moves between authorized Activity/Workbench hosts. Each independent file preview owns one local companion after first use. Selection/paste/drop immediately edits the same intent; model discovery starts after paint without delaying caret focus. Only actual intent notes guide; no generated question/reply hint/placeholder.

entries.title: Flower read state
entries.summary: Redeven confirms reads per user from server version and actual local presentation. Old responses cannot restore already-cleared indicators; unseen activity stays unread. Temporary sync failures recover in background without blocking operations or inventing acknowledgements.

entries.title: Flower incremental live state
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical history/versions; Redeven authorizes one workspace stream into ThreadCache. UTF-8 growth changes only its item. Merge pages immediately,prune after completion,preserving creation/selection. [Startup](../architecture/flower-startup-presentation.md) accepts first page,confirmed empty or selected detail,never partial Ready.

entries.title: Flower timeline ordering
entries.summary: Flower renders Floret ordered facts using stable item, TurnID and RunID identities. Captured ordinary input appears immediately; only that draft is consumed. Queued inputs stay in the dock. Canonical request-key confirmation preserves mounted rows without duplicates, and summaries never author timeline detail.

entries.title: Flower turn status and process disclosure
entries.summary: Floret owns exact TurnID/RunID, optional control kind, lifecycle/timing, intermediate/final IDs and complete-final boundary. Typed structure alone permits folding; prompts/summaries/time heuristics do not.

entries.title: Flower personal conversation preferences
entries.summary: Explicit model, directory and model-owned reasoning choices are remembered per authenticated namespace, endpoint and user. The originating surface consumes its authoritative response/settings revision without reloading shared model resources; other surfaces refresh persisted preferences.

entries.title: Flower model and navigation presentation
entries.summary: Flower separates Desktop/environment sources, unavailable models and first setup. Transient action failures use notifications; canonical failures remain in their timeline. The model picker aligns to the logical start edge of its trigger through the published Floe anchored-layer API, retaining surface boundary clamping.

entries.title: Flower setup and settings
entries.summary: Shared setup/settings serve both Flower carriers. The unconfigured surface is one open, canvas-level composition using published Floe ink and Button interaction, with no card, icon tile, heavy heading or filled call-to-action. It contains the Flower mark, setup title, one short explanation and the available settings destinations.

entries.title: Flower provider setup and account selection
entries.summary: Provider dialogs keep explicit access methods, keys, accounts and model selection independent. Use short names and access labels. Explain keys, quotas and saved methods in the access tooltip; model limits in the model tooltip. Icon links open official guidance.

entries.title: Flower failure recovery
entries.summary: Floret owns outcomes/checkpoints/migration. Transport uncertainty permits no replay. Readiness timeout offers refresh; deterministic migration failure remains administrative. Malformed model arguments use Floret's existing bounded correction before a question or Activity can appear.

entries.title: Flower composer attachments
entries.summary: One Flower controller owns attachment select/paste/drop/retry/remove/preview/send. The chat toolbar always retains its leftmost Plus attachment button. Thread-detail loads, model-capability refreshes and temporary editing restrictions disable it without removing its DOM node or shifting the toolbar.

entries.title: Flower consecutive tool sequences
entries.summary: Desktop/Env group consecutive tools/adjacent thinking. Prose/users/interactions/compaction/approvals/non-tool errors/Goal updates break groups; Goal/Web Search calls remain tools. Scoped child calls/reports/completion/attention/waits join; unknown parent/other waits break.

entries.title: Flower activity disclosure interaction
entries.summary: Desktop and Env App render canonical Floret facts with one transcript viewport owner. Canceled gestures activate nothing; disposal releases gesture ownership while retained content stays inspectable. Identity=thread/run/turn/canonical item. [Sequences](flower-tool-sequences.md) groups tools/thinking; individual details stay accessible.

entries.title: Flower conversation sidebar
entries.summary: Shared Desktop/Env rows are ThreadID-owned, pins endpoint-owned and details canonical ThreadCache-owned. Copy selection uses captured text after focus changes; explicit Copy message normalizes only that message. Weak row identity avoids transcript/backend scans.

entries.title: Flower inline media
entries.summary: Shared Flower renders canonical images/video/audio/screenshots/self-contained HTML through released Floe media/isolation. Ready HTML exposes direct authorized file/floating expansion plus source/more in a compact top row. Until ready, expansion is disabled; controls/insets cannot cover content.

entries.title: Flower streaming stability
entries.summary: Indexed ThreadCache and published incremental Markdown apply actor-native changes only to affected text/DOM. Structural scans use immutable identity without opening retained proxies;rows keep reactive owners,not plain-snapshot getters. Prompt history observes user content/status only;Activity counts follow replaced blocks.

entries.title: Flower progress and provisional edit presentation
entries.summary: Floret request facts drive output indicators; frozen tool schemas drive bounded provisional names/counts. Actual result names and counts replace previews on settlement. A failed patch shows only confirmed mutation diffs before its error, retaining the error status and stable disclosure row.

entries.title: Markdown diagram rendering
entries.summary: Flower and file Markdown preserve authored Mermaid while consuming published Floe/Pele. Only complete Mermaid fences become diagrams in streaming Flower Markdown. Incomplete fences remain readable and copyable code. Closing a fence creates one diagram owner; subsequent prose, terminal completion and identical snapshot regions preserve its SVG, focus and selection.

entries.title: Flower code highlighting
entries.summary: Flower owns committed Markdown lifetime; Floe enhanceCodeBlock owns visible tokenization/scheduling/color. Completed labelled fences receive colors in Env App/Desktop while source stays readable/copyable. Highlighting preserves geometry, focus and selection; unavailable or excessive work leaves plain code.

entries.title: Flower message appearance
entries.summary: Shared Flower uses Floe colors for compact reading and contrasting sent-message selection. Answered receipts retain every complete question followed by its answer in canonical order, without disclosure or choices. Questions use regular weight, answers medium weight, and a quiet check accompanies the localized status.

entries.title: Flower terminal activity presentation
entries.summary: Flower renders canonical Floret Activity with host task labels and safe details for every terminal operation, including writes/empty reads. Disclosure/scroll are ephemeral; no stdin/private paths/effect internals or invented lifecycle. An omitted output field is pending content, never an empty canonical frame with a nonzero first sequence.

entries.title: Shared interface scale
entries.summary: Published Floe owns type, controls and responsive rows; Redeven maps semantic roles without root scaling or a separate density setting. Desktop uses 13px body/control, 12px supporting and 11px captions. Published group spacing comes from role tokens. Measure real published components after fonts load, recording source/package identity, font, root, DPR and zoom.

entries.title: Flower decisions, approval presentation and secret drafts
entries.summary: Canonical Floret input and approval requests determine decision visibility and settlement. Result content loss and child attention do not themselves create parent confirmation controls. The UI shows canonical tool Activity and actual input/approval requests; only real model-requested observation produces verification activity.

entries.title: Flower citations
entries.summary: Floret stores assistant sources with end-exclusive Unicode code-point ranges. Only safe credential-free HTTP(S) URLs link; marker IDs imply no URL. Provider/gateway annotations preserve title, URL and optional positions. Floret validates and binds them to canonical assistant fragments for current/historical projections.

entries.title: Flower child task navigation and detail window
entries.summary: Authorized parent inventory controls child navigation; canonical thread identity chooses portraits and task labels. Single-target operations place the compact portrait/name capsule beside the action title. A deferred target field reserves the same line from its summary, before action or identity reads finish.

entries.title: Flower parent event timeline
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical child reports/events and admission; UI owns pages/bodies/disclosure only. Reading wakes neither task. Every full read rechecks recipient authority and canonical fixed-range paging. The parent transcript merges messages, anchored decorations and events by published canonical_ordinal on the queried Path; received time is display-only.

entries.title: Flower computer viewer presentation
entries.summary: Floe owns Stage geometry/launcher; Flower projects canonical status and decoded media. Viewing, moving, closing or restoring grants no target/execution authority. Interrupted/private frames retain recovery and cannot borrow unrelated images. The media contract remains the sole authorization/sampling owner.

entries.title: Flower working files and deliverables
entries.summary: Intermediates belong to Runtime state; finals to requested destination. Private roots grant no sibling authority. [Filesystem policy](tool-permission-runtime.md) governs all tools; cwd resolves paths only. Publish settings/validated canonical upload claims transactionally under source-deletion gate.

entries.title: Flower MCP runtime
entries.summary: Redeven configures MCP over official Go SDK stdio/Streamable HTTP sessions; Floret owns invocation/approval/effects/history/recovery. Package-owned connections project from the [Agent Plugins registry](flower-agent-plugins.md). They use the same SDK/session and Floret invocation paths, with separate credentials and explicit discovery.

entries.title: Flower Agent Plugins
entries.summary: Flower loads environment-scoped Agent Plugins1.0.0 Skills/MCP, separate from native .redevplugin SDK/packages/market. Root plugin.json uses https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json, validated locally; diagnose unknown top-level fields,ignore foreign namespaces.

entries.title: Flower plugin catalog integration
entries.summary: Flower can consume an explicitly configured plugin directory without shipping or maintaining a default index. Limits:16sources,1 MiB, IDs plugin-name syntax≤128characters, names nonempty single-line≤128Unicode, unique IDs/URLs. HTTPS host required; reject userinfo/query/fragment/unknown fields/malformed config explicitly.

entries.title: Flower thread Goals
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical Goal, model tool, reflection and completion; Redeven authorizes and presents facts. Stop/navigation/recovery remain usable; unresolved requests never imply successful mutation. Stop cancels execution and reflection; deletion only cancels future Goal checks.

entries.title: Tessiven Flower tools and scoped Runtime operations
entries.summary: Flower maps authorized code, configuration and Runtime facts into canvas versions. For tessiven_manage_instance, open prepares and returns entrance information for the running bound service and may run its preparation hook. It does not launch a browser or start a stopped service.

entries.title: Authorized platform model gateway
entries.summary: Redeven discovers authorized models via trusted control-channel lease/origin; Runtime never receives platform Provider keys. Floret owns execution/tools/history/recovery; platform Edge admission/binding/reservations/accounting. A removed model stays unavailable instead of silently switching an existing thread.

entries.title: Model directory and selection
entries.summary: Runtime owns atomic metadata. Background refresh is disclosed, opt-in and excludes OpenRouter. Runtime uses `runtime/model-catalog` and resolves shipped defaults on read. Identity-only unreviewed models require configuration. OpenAI-compatible inventories use Floret's public `ParseOpenAIModelMetadata`.

entries.title: Model web search
entries.summary: Redeven resolves provider/model search preferences once for settings and turns; final tools drive prompt/wire. Floret v7.40.2 validates hosted events against frozen requests. Undeclared hosted execution fails because remote effects cannot safely be assumed absent.

entries.title: Local ChatGPT admission and account lifecycle
entries.summary: Authenticated local capability and verified account facts govern ChatGPT registration, renewal and requests. Interrupted logout is completed at startup; normal maintenance scans never clear a live logout. Account updates use model_directory.changed and merge independently of drafts.

entries.title: Provider configuration validation
entries.summary: Redeven owns configuration, credentials and Flower readiness across every settings entrypoint and provider-bundle save. Floret's public runtime contract is unchanged. Invalid saves preserve configuration and credentials; authentication/network failures remain execution errors.

entries.title: Provider API and catalog review
entries.summary: Runtime/Web/Desktop/iOS share an authenticated reviewed catalog. Pinned models.dev inventory and official contracts require released adapters plus qualified limits/replay/tools/images/reasoning. Refresh preserves selections/conversation identities. Review dates: October12 baseline, October24 Kimi; no audio/video/embeddings/restricted models.

entries.title: Direct image reading and tool media retention
entries.summary:
image_read inspects authorized files/snapshots. File references stay references; results use native
images, not browsers, temporary servers or Base64 result JSON. One in-process media gate protects writes and the complete canonical inventory through deletion, following Floret's published retention contract.

entries.title: AI tool runtime and canonical interaction ownership
entries.summary: Redeven supplies typed product tools, policies, effects and presentation; Floret owns invocation, irreversible intent, approvals and admitted history. Lease release follows the canonical terminal view, not the HTTP response or Desktop connection lifetime, so an existing session cannot admit hidden work after the final lifecycle snapshot.

entries.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical Agent formats; Redeven owns product facts and uploads. Unknown, future, drifted or invalid state blocks Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime. Floret owns bounded startup recognition and background per-thread migration.

entries.title: Flower storage recovery and retired backups
entries.summary: Ordinary startup and migrations do not create full Flower backups. Settings exposes runtime status and diagnostics, not obsolete snapshot browsing or restore controls.

entries.title: Flower historical writer acceptance
entries.summary: Immutable fixtures come from locked released Redeven writers; current tests copy and verify them. The released Floret v7.102.0 host-work fixture also qualifies unknown-outcome history through the public runtime and Redeven DTO. Browser acceptance exercises the same serialized Activity contract.

entries.title: Flower attachment resources
entries.summary: Redeven owns authenticated bytes/metadata/quotas/retention; Floret turn membership. Upload once, submit opaque attachment_id, render attachment://v1 and revalidate provider resources. Admit files independently of model modalities/tools. Preserve recognized text/image/PDF types; other files, including Office and non-UTF-8 documents, keep original bytes/name as application/octet-stream.

entries.title: AI tool permissions and dispatch
entries.summary: Redeven owns visibility/policy/prompts/approval UI; Floret owns invocation and neutral tools. Retired Todo remains readable but unavailable; [Goals](flower-goals.md) retains its own owner. File inspection shares current scope across modes.

entries.title: Computer and browser use runtime
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns targets, resources, control and script processes; Floret owns Agent lifecycle/effects/history. Prefer authorized commands for data, semantics for interaction and images for visual decisions. Stage viewing uses its independent bounded sampler; those samples never enter model history.

entries.title: Computer semantic snapshots
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime normalizes browser, macOS AX and Linux AT-SPI facts into bounded schema v2. Browser role resolution scans the complete authorized AX scope independently of the bounded model observation. A unique control after node 1000 remains resolvable; a duplicate beyond the presentation boundary remains ambiguous.

entries.title: Computer script execution and semantic observations
entries.summary: One computer_exec is one Floret effect attempt. Every operation rechecks target/grant/cancel/control. Canonical turn retains target during live sampling; changed target/permission stops confirmed prefix. Private/approval consent binds exact target/URL/lease.

entries.title: Computer script read and validation boundaries
entries.summary: Reads return promised shapes or explicit failures, never fabricated empty observations. Typed preflight document/candidate invalidation with no preparation/input returns not_dispatched, seals invocation and adds no completed_actions. [Scripts](computer-use-scripts.md) owns namespace/failure barriers; every read retains privacy/permission/publication checks.

entries.title: Computer source detail and continuation reads
entries.summary:
Source reads make original AX/DOM fields and descendants reachable beyond the
bounded default tree. [Read validation](computer-script-read-contract.md) owns
permissions, privacy and final publication; source detail does not bypass it or grant new target authority.

entries.title: Optional built-in browser installation
entries.summary: Runtime owns optional Chromium installation, enabled by default but downloaded only after authenticated confirmation. Disable cancels/closes/blocks prompts while retaining bytes/site data. Floret owns waiting/continuation; failed verification publishes nothing and exposes Retry/source choice.

entries.title: Built-in browser Linux system preparation
entries.summary: Installation manager owns readiness; short approved Runtime transactions prepare Linux namespaces/dependencies. Preserve sandbox/global AppArmor and admit only catalog bytes at fixed root-owned paths. Neither `--no-sandbox`, global AppArmor changes nor exemptions for replaceable user-owned executables are permitted.

entries.title: Browser and desktop settings
entries.summary: Both carriers share Browser and desktop settings. Runtime capabilities, thread grants and extension consent are independent. The browser page presents connected profiles with their actual Chrome/Chromium marks, inline connection status, and a shared connect/refresh action row.

entries.title: Guided personal browser connection
entries.summary: Desktop and Env App share browser connection guidance over ComputerUseRuntime and Floret interactions. Users confirm Chrome installation and initial binding; later sessions restore the same environment. Active failed operations retain connection_diagnostic:{phase:source_disconnected, reason} from their exact extension source lifetime.

entries.title: Chrome connection diagnostics and recovery
entries.summary: Runtime owns readiness/handshakes; both carriers provide host-specific recovery. Installed Chrome/accepted launch proves neither control nor continuation. Browser target selection belongs to Flower; no separate browser source preference or product database is read during startup.

entries.title: Managed browsers and authorized Chrome tabs
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns connection, authorization and control for managed Chromium, explicit CDP and Chrome extension through one restricted executor. Explicit Browser and desktop connection/tab creation selects the conversation target. Approval Required binds current target/URL; temporary URL authority never becomes saved origin permission.

entries.title: Semantic desktop operations and explicit control
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns desktop execution: explicit macOS app window or private Linux Xvfb/D-Bus. Application discovery reuses HostApplicationCatalog; exact candidate selection uses NSWorkspace with current app/foreground permission. Launch completion is synchronized, cancellation stops further actions, and window readiness is bounded.

entries.title: Computer target selection across threads
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns discovery/selection through Flower's computer tools. Stale/disconnected/occupied targets fail explicitly while retaining previous selection. Set application to a name or bundle ID for bounded installed-app discovery, including apps not running.

entries.title: Computer use safety pauses and user control
entries.summary: Floret owns questions, answers and continuation; Redeven owns authorized computer effects and private media. Answers pass unchanged without granting authority or replay. Password controls establish secret_input, not login intent. Existing explicit login consumers remain supported.

entries.title: Private browser observation and input
entries.summary: Runtime owns observer-bound private pixels/input; Floret takeover/continuation. Bind observer/revision/thread/run/target; disconnect revokes and uncertainty never replays. Canonical answer starts a fresh Run/observation; private input also waits for matching decoded pixels.

entries.title: Computer use media and visual requests
entries.summary:
Redeven owns authorized screenshots; Floret owns history/preparation. Durable frames and ephemeral samples have separate
lifetimes; tool success does not prove delivery. Each controller holds one model anchor. Viewer sampling cannot replace it. Changed target, document, viewport, bounds or observed native accessibility state rejects stale input.

entries.title: Computer use product qualification
entries.summary: Qualify Computer through built renderer/Runtime/decoder/target adapter with default tools (explicit legacy-wait excepted). Cover output/budgets/prefixes, pre-focus validation, paging/images, delays/titles/staleness, scroll/conditions, async text/landmarks/reset, scripts/downloads and native entry.

entries.title: Computer use provider qualification evidence
entries.summary: Historical runs support [qualification](computer-use-qualification.md) only for their declared platform, provider and build scope. Canonical results and independently observed effects establish execution. Original model, measurement and transport failures remain distinct from subsequent passing runs; no result certifies arbitrary applications.

entries.title: Computer use qualification evidence
entries.summary: Historical runs follow [the acceptance contract](computer-use-qualification.md). Worktree passes do not replace exact-main checks, certify arbitrary applications or erase failures. Retained diagnostics exclude private text and pixels. Each result keeps its original platform, source identity, acceptance boundary and unresolved limitations.

entries.title: Browser and native drag timing qualification
entries.summary:
Browser drag timing is measured from actual input events, with all model and
assertion failures retained. [Script contracts](computer-use-scripts.md) define
behavior; [qualification](computer-use-qualification.md) defines the test lane.
Browser measurements certify only the tested browser paths and durations.

entries.title: Media contention and native read qualification
entries.summary:
The October 28 qualification validates cancellable media-write admission and
native node/subtree completeness. Production uses published Floret v7.88.0;
its existing cancellable inventory and write-gate contract need no upstream
change. Browser, AX and AT-SPI share the same completeness semantics.

entries.title: Computer use paired model measurements
entries.summary: Paired production Flower/Floret/model/browser fixtures compare visual primitives with semantic scripts on the same tasks. Keep all failures and reject missing, duplicate or unmeasured samples. Headless results do not certify native desktop or Chrome focus; those require separate product qualification.

entries.title: Codex computer and browser use design evidence
entries.summary: Versioned official documentation and installed app 26.908.40834/extension 1.26.901.11451 inform command-first routing, AX/script batching and compact observations. They expose neither proprietary implementation nor universal external-window isolation. Flower Runtime remains execution and authorization authority.

entries.title: AI terminal tool runtime
entries.summary: Redeven owns PTYs and bounded output; Floret v7 owns canonical tool calls, interactions, effect attempts, results and Activity. [Task-file placement](flower-task-files.md) supplies thread scratch/staging through child-only environment variables while preserving project cwd and OS temporary path conventions.

entries.title: Model reasoning capability, selection and transport
entries.summary: One capability catalog and canonicalizer define reasoning controls for saved threads and immutable turns. [Preferences](../ui/flower-conversation-preferences.md) own explicit full-model-identity choices and budgets. Sending/automatic normalization cannot save them; preference failure reports separately without rolling back confirmed thread settings or changing retry snapshots.

entries.title: Flower prompt and rule sources
entries.summary: Every Flower run profile shares one host English base prompt defining Redeven assistant identity, visual output and local delivery. Visual output uses the existing [inline HTML preview](../ui/flower-inline-media.md) contract when it communicates better than text; ordinary nonvisual answers remain text.

entries.title: AI model and context runtime
entries.summary: Redeven persists model/reasoning preferences, credentials and source selection. Token input/output limits remain separate and configuration merges preserve unrelated settings. The comparison logs are /tmp/redeven-budget-desktop-failures-focused.log and /tmp/redeven-budget-desktop-main-baseline.log.

entries.title: Model provider surface and history
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical provider history/rendering lineage; Redeven supplies models, prompts, permissions and ephemeral overlays. Hosted search projects action.sources URLs into Activity; Qwen retains its own shape. Published ResponsesOutput reconciles done and terminal events.

entries.title: Model request recovery
entries.summary: Floret owns retry admission, physical-request deadlines and attempt identity. Published Floret v7.58.0 shares provider.RetryAdviceForError across direct and Desktop paths. Adapter-owned response checks use typed diagnostic codes and reviewed constant messages for output conflicts or gaps, tool namespace/argument conflicts, invalid usage and native history preparation/commit failures.

entries.title: Model request reuse
entries.summary: Floret owns reuse decisions/canonical state; Redeven runs one prepared request/Responses consumer. Failure follows ordinary turn recovery; supplemental context never enables reuse. Runtime/Desktop epoch 68 and model-source RPC v4 preserve Floret's effective request reuse policy.

entries.title: Context usage, measurement and compaction
entries.summary: Floret owns confirmed usage, pressure, bounded compaction and canonical installation. Redeven projects independent token/byte/image evidence; exact image counts/decoded bytes retain preparation/response stage and never occupy another unit's fields.

entries.title: DeepSeek Responses
entries.summary:
Flower routes the DeepSeek provider to the published Floret v7.66.1 Responses gateway. Floret owns `/responses` rendering, SSE parsing, reasoning, usage normalization,
function-call validation, and opaque provider history. Each request sends full input history.

entries.title: Flower canonical thread queries
entries.summary:
Flower exposes two read-only tools for finding another readable conversation
and reading its content: `thread_query` and `thread_read`. The tool contract
is intentionally smaller than Floret's published general query API.
`threads.aggregate` is not registered or dispatched.

entries.title: Floret thread runtime integration
entries.summary: Floret v7 ThreadService alone owns active/canonical lifecycle. Redeven authorizes endpoints/resources/provider-tool effects. Send/Respond/Cancel/Retry/CompactContext return typed state before continuation. Floret owns one-time historical source preparation during upgrade.

entries.title: Floret Redeven adapter and projection
entries.summary: Redeven authorizes ownership/resources and maps typed Floret views, updates, failures and safe Activity. Root/child/command receipts share bounded windows containing canonical Summary in the same baseline. No separately sampled preparation/watermark. Authorized history POST installs interest on the ordered observer; item POST expands only published frozen-live/manifest/hash-verified locators.

entries.title: Flower child runtime and parent event boundary
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical child threads, reports and parent events. Its flat provider schema requires spawn(task_name,task_description,message), send_input(target,message), close(target) and wait(ids); status/inspect deduplicate target then ids.

entries.title: Flower thread Fork and deletion coordination
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical Fork and deletion; Redeven authorizes endpoint scope and coordinates product settings, read state and file claims. Convergence uses typed canonical outcomes without a saga, compensating deletion or cross-database atomicity claim.

entries.title: Flower plugin generation
entries.summary: Flower authors through released ReDevPlugin CLI/SDK and version-matched guidance. Plugin Center owns authoring conversations; ordinary Flower keeps its tools/navigation. Canonical streaming, approvals and dispatch stay shared.

entries.title: Plugin build visibility
entries.summary: Proposed upstream build progress, not shipped behavior. Keep one canvas, preview authority and compact status control. Existing first-artifact auto-preview and early runnable milestones need no new platform API; deliver the requested layout and a useful interaction with labeled examples or explicit missing-data states.

entries.title: Redeven environment operations
entries.summary: Environment lifecycle goes through Redeven product operations, never guessed container/SSH/systemd/launchctl/process commands. Flower receives this rule from the standard redeven-environment skill; do not embed a second environment workflow into the global prompt.

entries.title: OKF bundle lifecycle
entries.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

entries.title: OKF tool suite
entries.summary: Redeven exposes the embedded OKF bundle through read-only `okf_get_index`, `okf_search`, and `okf_open` builtin tools. Redeven projects bounded safe results into Floret v7.26.0 structured Activity rows, and the shared Flower surface expands those rows without reading raw OKF result JSON.

entries.title: Flower managed runtime facts
entries.summary: Floret v7.47.1 owns chronological admission, semantic updates, context messages, compaction and recovery.
