concepts.summary: Redeven owns authenticated bytes/metadata/quotas/retention; Floret turn membership. Upload once, submit opaque attachment_id, render attachment://v1 and revalidate provider resources. Admit files independently of model modalities/tools. Preserve recognized text/image/PDF types; other files, including Office and non-UTF-8 documents, keep original bytes/name as application/octet-stream.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and provider preparation
Redeven product threadstore v1 owns generated attachment ID, authenticated user hash, private relative storage name, detected/sanitized media metadata, exact size/SHA-256, optional strict UTF-8 code-point/line counts, source/state/idempotency and retention claims. Floret ResourceRef is content-addressed; display locator is attachment://v1/<attachment-id>/<encoded-name>. Retention never authorizes canonical reads.

Active UTF-8 uses text/plain; pasted long text requires strict UTF-8. Queue/admission enforce owner, staging, count and byte bounds, not a model MIME allowlist.

Capabilities affect presentation only. Supported modalities receive native content; otherwise the owning user message/tool result receives a factual manifest: name, media_type, size_bytes, locator, content_included:false, content_trust:untrusted. It adds no system message, tool-selection instruction or generic failure advice. Tool definitions own access guidance; manifest implies neither extraction, tool availability nor parser installation. The model chooses tools or explains its limitation. Switching models never rejects retained attachments/images; verify canonical descriptors/digest before the same manifest fallback, preserving native rendering for capable models.

## Reads and copies
Historical reads revalidate membership and bytes. Upload/image lookup uses current-path public Floret windows (50 items, 128-byte previews), one authorized subscription and page/stable-leaf correlation; no full hydration or retention-inventory authorization. Resolved handles prove ownership/metadata only. Hash during materialization; provider/text/image consumers verify their exact snapshots and downloads verify before returning paths. Avoid prehash plus reread. Bound size/cancellation; corrupt bytes never publish a copy.

Floret v7.51.1 exposes user and confirmed tool descriptors canonically. Retention distinguishes tool media from uploads; never parse image refs as upload rows.

attachment_materialize requires current execution/canonical authorization, RWX and normal write policy. Create a unique regular scratch copy using cancellable 32 KiB streaming with exact size/SHA-256; image locators retain bounded validation. Failure deletes private staging, repeated names never overwrite edited copies, and output exposes only the work path.

## Lifetime
Cleanup removes work copies, never original inputs/images. Retained references permit rematerialization after cleanup/restart/compaction/parent deletion. Historical Fork inherits refs only through its canonical cut and separately copies current scratch/staging. Product settings/claims publish transactionally without another admitted-message map.

Files derives input/media pages from public windows with current product authorization. Last-reference inventory includes inactive paths/queued inputs but grants no read authority. External files/deliveries retain destinations and survive cleanup. Existing upload/media backup scope excludes disposable task files.

Both the server proxy allowlist and Floe's browser response policy explicitly retain

Redeven does not inspect or migrate Floret storage, persist message ordering, expose a filesystem path, accept a client owner, authorize by locator, or infer canonical membership from its claim table. Neither transport embeds bytes or a URL identity in a turn JSON body.

## Retired automatic snapshots
The public snapshot-list and restore APIs are removed. Successful activation and startup preparation admit one background cleanup of checksum-verified, unprotected automatic snapshots only. Cleanup checks cancellation, refuses a pending replacement journal, pins the snapshot directory, and never traverses links. Unknown, damaged, protected and before-restore records remain unchanged. Cleanup failure cannot block healthy conversations.

No cleanup targets live conversations, uploads, read state, extension configuration, or opaque upstream stores. Filesystem statistics do not certify backups.

## Durable recovery and diagnostics
Previously admitted durable replacements must finish and verify before opening another generation. A failed generation close fences recovery. Abandoned staging retires only after replacement completes.

The diagnostic settings category retains actual runtime status, safe retry/stop, sanitized diagnostics and explicit orphan ownership review. Diagnostics omit conversations, credentials, database contents and uploads. There is no generic deletion API or backup-success claim.

## Compaction and continuation
[Manual compaction](model-context-usage-and-compaction.md#manual-compaction) defaults to explicit continue_goal intent. Retry and restart use canonical preparation and confirmed tools. Redeven forwards intent and renders state without a second execution coordinator.

## Goal ownership and execution
User and model updates enter Floret's shared journal writer with request identity and expected version. An existing unfinished Goal remains authoritative across continuation and context restoration.

## Interaction and recovery
Selecting or entering /goal opens an in-composer command chip.
The chip shares the editor's typography and first line box. Entering, typing a
single-line Goal and exiting preserve composer, footer and transcript geometry;
multiline text retains normal bounded autosizing. Native command conversion
synchronizes the editable value even when the canonical draft stays empty, so
the localized Goal placeholder appears immediately.

Each popup opening confirms detail through the existing read coordinator before showing canonical text.

A failed binding leaves the draft available for retry; no cross-thread target validation is relaxed and no attachment is uploaded twice.

## Optional runtime configuration
REDEVEN_AGENT_AI_PLUGIN_CATALOGS is a runtime-process JSON array of {id, name, url}; unset/whitespace/[] means none. Example:team/Team extensions/https://catalog.example.com/plugins.json, never a default. Restart applies config. No official URL, startup fetch/search/remote switch/automatic enrollment.

Network checks occur only when browsing through bounded public distribution.

Configured sources use configured:<id>/managed:true and memory only. User UUID/CAS sources retain independent 16 limit. Configured URLs take display precedence without deleting user records; removal reveals retained source. User APIs cannot delete configured sources. Config changes do not revise installation registry or alter snapshots/credentials/data. Desktop/Web use authenticated runtime routes; renderer-only environment has no effect.

## Directory document
flower.agent_plugin_catalog.v1 contains directory id/plugins; entry{id, optional display, source{type:github, repository, ref, path}}. IDs follow plugin-name syntax≤128; unique entry IDs. Limits 128entries/1 MiB, reject overflow rather than truncate. Empty[] valid; missing/null arrays, unsupported schema, trailing JSON/unknown top-level-entry-source fields reject. display alone allows discarded additive fields:single-line name/author≤128Unicode, description≤512. Render text only, no HTML/badges/credentials/configuration. Incompatible changes need a new schema.

Existing public-GitHub normalizer validates repository/ref/commit/path (default .). Different repository paths stay independent installs. Catalog identity/removal never changes installed identity/state.

## Browse and install boundary
Browse reads bounded JSON only, no archive/preparation/process/enablement. Install invokes the existing manual-GitHub preparation:resolve exact revision, snapshot package, validate real manifest/components. Preview uses actual metadata, not directory claims; commit binds reviewed digest/explicit selection. Listing/topic/manifest is no endorsement.

Fetch failure exposes Retry, not empty success. Unconfigured/unavailable/removed discovery cannot affect installed management/execution. [Extensions](../ui/flower-extensions.md) owns UI; [Agent Plugins](flower-agent-plugins.md) owns snapshots/permissions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Guidance and upstream workflow
Only authenticated active plugin-creation conversations discover/activate `redeven-plugin-authoring` and `plugin_author_*` tools. Ordinary model requests omit both; Settings may browse/disable the skill. Activation/dispatch retain normal permissions. Installation coordinate follows imported ReDevPlugin, without another pin.

Preserve the user's project identity/data contracts; new projects choose the smallest suitable released template. Pure Web surfaces may use declared private resources without a Worker. Worker execution requires published WASM tooling and verified development runtime. Missing capabilities remain explicit requirements.

Released ReDevPlugin owns doctor diagnostics, generation/typecheck/build/business-test/package pipeline, watching, persistent development roots, candidates, fresh session authority, connections review and runtime preparation. Flower consumes actual reports, never duplicates validators/watchers/lifecycle/supervisor. Doctor/package/business evidence is not browser or WASM proof; qualify requested journeys and state verified boundaries.

Candidates build while current frame/drafts remain; Apply/reload creates a fresh frame and needs saved application state. Failed builds retain valid preview. Persistent roots survive restart; reset is explicitly destructive. Connections retain destination review/grants/revocation.

## Draft and conversation ownership
Each draft owns one canonical Flower conversation and opaque platform workspace. Ordinary paginated/live inventories exclude all owned threads, including deleting/deleted records, independently of title/directory/backend availability; pagination crosses hidden pages. Reconnect empty baselines preserve embedded selected detail/composer/live updates. Explicit references to ordinary threads never adopt/delete them.

Use ordinary composer Send, attachments, approvals, streaming and dispatch; no direct-creation intent/fallback prompt. `/plugin` navigates before model configuration and never becomes a turn when unavailable. Initial reference attaches only to the first new-thread submission and clears on acceptance.

Authenticated runs resolve the `plugin.author` profile into the shared `work_binding` canonical `ModelContextSnapshot` section; Floret compares/adopts chronologically. Unchanged guidance is not another user reference; ordinary threads omit it and persisted history stays intact.

Draft turns/input/approval/compaction/goal continuations use authenticated environment HTTP, never synthetic Local UI authority. Owner is authenticated user/environment. Freeze exact canonical create request before creating thread; bind ownership before root settings. Reused IDs cannot adopt unrelated threads/projects. Reopen/delete reconciles interrupted settings admission under that same request without replaying a user turn.

Only platform-resolved authenticated managed source joins filesystem scope; preserve private task-file isolation and ordinary file/terminal effect approvals. Other projects/platform state/task directories stay excluded. Admitted source work survives disconnect under original user/environment/current tool policy without reactivating expired platform sessions. Explicit Retry binds current authenticated channel authority while preserving model/options and failed record. Build/capture may finish offline; installation readiness is session-bound and re-reviewed on reconnect. Acceptance covers post-disconnect tools/context refresh, retry and long history.

`plugin_author_get_status`, initialize, rename, build and capture require the owned thread. Initialize persists selected title; Flower chooses concise localized names unless user supplied one. Rename binds revision/owner/thread; source display name/build is separate from installed authority. Status retains structured metadata despite long-log truncation. Legacy unnamed history uses verified package names without rewriting titles.

Changed release bytes need higher source SemVer, preserving identity. Build/capture use released Host inspection against formal installation, returning `ready_for_install` and structured `installation_check` even with truncated logs. Rejected packages need repair; same-version preview iteration remains allowed. Readiness cannot install/grant/change frames. Build is a normal Floret command effect; retained stages distinguish passed/failed/interrupted/not-run. Packaging alone proves neither business correctness nor browser behavior.

For iterative work, guidance requests a small useful runnable version and early validated build; first artifact may auto-apply, later updates stay explicit. This is guidance, not guaranteed latency or scheduling. Unrelated demos, untouched template captures or unlabeled fabricated data are not progress. Simple edits need no milestone build; preview never replaces completion/acceptance. [Build visibility](../ui/plugin-build-visibility.md) remains a proposal, not shipped events/UI.

Deletion durably freezes admission, reconciles pending create, cancels/deletes the owned thread, then closes/removes platform workspace. Interrupted cleanup resumes its stage. Unknown formal install outcomes must reconcile before removal; installed instances remain. Legacy direct deletion follows the same review/cleanup.

## Visual revision and delivery
Canvas comments enter the same thread through durable outbox with explicit text and bounded reviewed-artifact context. Preserve unrelated composer content. Active runs queue without stopping Flower. Comments supply only their visual context; package repair uses no synthetic workspace references. Dispatch waits for handler/storage generation; blocked/unknown decisions cannot launch a turn. Rejected/uncertain submissions retain ordinary recovery. Model reads current source via status; text/selectors are untrusted observations. Stale selectors never authorize blind edits/install; changed source may need reconciliation.

Before the first runnable milestone, author a purpose-specific self-contained SVG at `ui/assets/plugin-icon.svg`; locked build renders/packages 256×256 PNG and SVG, with `presentation.icon.path=ui/assets/plugin-icon.png`. Configured tests verify alignment. Missing/invalid assets, stock placeholders or disguised rasters fail delivery. Inspect 16/24/32px in both themes; no active/external SVG resources. Preserve existing icon identity on unrelated edits.

This is Flower delivery policy, not global admission: platform still accepts PNG/WebP icons and rejects SVG surface icons. Consume verified raster evidence. Model-instruction/generated-artifact tests cover policy; shared conversion or SVG admission requires upstream release.

Authorized local project steps use ordinary tools; final sources/packages go to user's destination. Plugin Center inspects exact bytes for installation review/confirmation. Install approval, execution grants and auto-update eligibility remain separate. Ordinary plugin packages need no publisher trust/signature admission; platform/runtime releases retain verification. No second approval wait, Floret bypass, manual timeline mutation or audit-to-activity conversion. Unknown effects reconcile; requested approvals wait for canonical resolution.

concepts.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations
concepts.summary: Floret owns canonical Agent formats; Redeven owns product facts and uploads. Unknown, future, drifted or invalid state blocks Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime. Floret owns bounded startup recognition and background per-thread migration.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Storage owners
Redeven consumes the exact published Floret version in go.mod with `GOWORK=off`.

Each validated dependency closure publishes atomically; retained sources retire only after complete verification. The oldest v2-v5 snapshots reserve historical identities through a resumable scan before new-thread admission. Segmented stores admit new threads immediately. Redeven uses public status, thread preparation and per-thread media contracts and never decodes upstream records.

Published Floret v7.87.0 removes hidden Activity field preparation from ordinary startup, retains summary metadata on large activity admission, batches explicit locator writes and skips same-value SQLite upserts. Its recent manifest cache is bounded, memory-only and owned upstream. No new host indexes, full-text indexes or duplicate conversation storage are introduced. First disclosure may still prepare the selected complete activity once; this is not a claim of field-granular cold preparation.

Cancellation, shutdown and execution-context settlement resolve canonical control records through Floret. The host keeps the original Stop request and does not read or reconstruct upstream conversation bodies to settle it.

Flower freezes the displayed `turn_id` and `run_id` with one `client_request_id`
at Stop click time. Desktop, Env App, HTTP and RPC pass these fields unchanged
to published Floret cancellation preconditions. An unconfirmed retry first
resynchronizes and retains the same target and key; if execution changed, it
resolves that old action without stopping the replacement. A fresh subsequent
click may target the new execution. Server-side stale targets return conflict.
Legacy internal callers may omit the complete optional target; partial targets
are rejected. Stop response remains acknowledgement-only; canonical views own
settlement. Existing stop presentation and copy are unchanged.

Floret projects canonical interrupted/cancelled terminal facts into subsequent
model context alongside retained partial output. The host adds no transcript
message or process-state claim. Restart, Fork, Retry, compaction and rendered
cache revision remain upstream-owned. Ordinary Stop preserves queued inputs;
Send now retains the explicit upstream stop-and-promote transition.


A read-state failure cannot become a core Runtime constructor failure or a synthetic read record.

Redeven also owns the [Agent Plugins registry](flower-agent-plugins.md), snapshots and installation data. Its schema-1 SQLite store is separate from canonical conversation history; credential references resolve through SecretsStore schema 4. Neither owner decodes Floret records.

## Execution configuration
Product schema 11 to 12 adds bounded execution configuration to the existing
admission authority. It retains original provider/model and RunOptions for
continuations; it is not a second lifecycle table. Historical rows remain valid
with no inferred configuration. Floret owns host-work facts, final output,
notice admission, unknown recovery and continuation identity.

## Readonly checks and owner transactions
`sqliteutil` owns WAL-aware readonly preflight, integrity checks and complete SQLite snapshots for product and read-state owners. Inspection never creates missing data or runs a migration.

Owner transactions migrate without full startup snapshots. The [recovery contract](flower-backup-and-recovery.md) governs completion of admitted replacements and retirement of obsolete automatic backups.

## Frozen historical queue conversion
The migration-only `pendinginputlegacy` package owns the complete interpretation of historical queue bytes: session identity, options, context shapes, default values, resource metadata and normalization limits.

The v4-to-v5 product transaction imports canonical pending inputs through Floret's public idempotent import API, records necessary product authority and removes retired source tables before commit. Owner versions and canonical records remain the progress authority; no build-driven snapshot journal is created.

## Resource and authorization retention
Product upload references retain resources for every canonical thread that contains them, including ordinary forks, nested forks and restored inputs.

After activation, product recovery pages settings, retains each thread's complete descriptors and promotes eligible admitted input. Failures retain the cleanup gate while independent threads recover. Tool-media collection keeps its complete global inventory, write gate and idle constraint.

Bounded keyset maintenance and compaction stop and drain with their owning generation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Placement and authority
Runtime owns StateDir/task-files/ThreadID/{scratch,staging}; finals use user's destination/project/worktree, independent of temporary cwd. Admission/provider context share absolute roots. System placement overrides skills without filename heuristics/new grants; ordinary source/test/build locations remain. Children receive FLOWER_SCRATCH_DIR/FLOWER_STAGING_DIR, never FLOWER_OUTPUT_DIR; cwd/HOME/cache/TMPDIR retain semantics. Reject escaping links/siblings without whitelisting authorized external roots.

## Fork and recovery
Fork copies current scratch/staging even at historical cut, not historical snapshots; project/finals stay shared. Block source admissions/cleanup, cancellably drain admitted work, reject unreaped processes. Rooted bounded copy preserves executable bits, checks identity/size/time/final tree, rejects external/hard links/unsupported types and renames complete private staging only.

Unadmitted copies remain invisible; canonical replay finishes publication without recopying admitted edits. Source markers survive cleanup until deletion and support interrupted context/publication. Recheck ownership before removing failed copies. Startup/periodic scans50names/batch, skips in-flight and removes private stages/marked forks without settings. Orphan actions share target gate. Retry preserves canonical identity with fresh copy. Context maps nested ancestor suffixes; inspect/repair hardcoded paths without rewriting history. Ancestor cleanup never deletes descendants.

## Delivery and discovery
file_present cancellably validates/hashes authorized regular files outside app state with identity/size/mtime checks; returns path/title/MIME/size/SHA256/mtime/endpoint/thread/turn/run without moving original. Files discovers canonical authorized successful results (50records/page,32KiB/record), retaining restart/Fork provenance without crawling/ledger. Availability checks unchanged size/mtime, no historical rehash; missing/changed/unavailable are observations.

Default deliveries/uploads; Process files separates tool images/temporary files without retention change. One controller advances50item/128byte-preview windows through empty/search pages until cursor end; viewport end drives reads. Initial sources may parallelize, then serialize. Repeated cursor offers Retry; temporary/child preview pauses discovery, no fullView/retention scans. Equal same-owner refresh preserves successful rows/focus/scroll. Scope change invalidates; close/change aborts discovery/preview/download reads and fences replies. Partial failure retains successes. Floe Dialog owns bounds/Tab/Escape/restoration; close retains query/filter/scroll, folder handoff closes. Env has rich renderers; Desktop image/PDF/text/Markdown/opaqueHTML, otherwise Download.

loadTaskFile validates endpoint and reauthorizes every256KiB, rejects version/offset drift, caps preview20MiB and streams downloads. Desktop permits exact thread endpoint/query keys with IPC cancel. Blob sinks retain memory costs; reads never publish original.

## Downloads and panel
Enqueue in Shell Downloads before destination: one Env topbar/Desktop full-companion owner. Deliveries/temporary use validated chunks; uploads/images use attachment reader. Retry binds original source/thread/runtime; metadata contains no URL/Blob. Manager owns destination/progress/cancel/failure/retry/completion. Thread/list changes stop previews, not admitted downloads; reopened lists check active downloads before cleanup. Late settlement cannot revive cancellation; finalization cannot cancel. Native destination offers Reveal/Open, browser handoff stays explicit. Retain until Shell exit/Clear finished, never import OS history.

Published controls/icons/tokens: title/close header, search/refresh body, filters only multiple known kinds, removed choice resets All. No ambiguous totals/empty headings/collapsed images/manual paging. Delivered means file_present. Preserve same-name image names/times. Keyboard rows show origin/size/lazy thumbnail/exceptional availability, hiding success badges/MIME parameters/IDs/absolute paths even in tooltip; paths remain action inputs. Phone labels wrap beside accessible download/folder/source.

Temporary files appears only when present, with Back/preview/confirmed cleanup; Process files has no blanket delete. Restore focus/scroll, active work/downloads block cleanup. Failed pages offer Retry beside retained data. Body alone scrolls in stable viewport; complete locales and [loading continuity](../ui/page-loading-continuity.md#page-continuity) apply.

## Cleanup/deletion
List<=200 after<=10000entries, disclose truncation/lower bound. Confirmed RWX cleanup pins owned roots, rejects symlinks/checks opened identity; path grants no delete authority. Active/queued turns/interactions/admitted work/unreaped terminals block via admissions/canonicalView. Deletion settles canonical work/stops owned terminals; force explicitly cancels. Resume settings cleanup only after Summary ErrThreadDeleted. Maintenance handles50settings/pass/bounded waits, advances failures/retries next cycle. Clean files before product/child records; remove anchors only after success.

Cleanup preserves uploads/images. Deletion releases claims while canonical retention protects queues/forks/references. Exclude finals; archive deletes nothing/noTTL. Disclose project-local state.

concepts.summary: Floret owns canonical Fork and deletion; Redeven authorizes endpoint scope and coordinates product settings, read state and file claims. Convergence uses typed canonical outcomes without a saga, compensating deletion or cross-database atomicity claim.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Fork
`ForkThreadWithOptions` validates RWX access, the source ThreadID, endpoint identity, and a stable `client_request_id`. The shared endpoint/thread authority boundary must find a live product settings row for that exact endpoint before any Floret call.

An optional `source_item_id` selects a committed assistant answer on the active path. Floret retains that answer and its preceding history while excluding later items. Answer-level Fork supplies this anchor; thread-list Fork omits it and retains the current full path. Invalid or uncommitted anchors fail explicitly.

Detail recovery retains the created destination and retries loading only.

## Deletion
The service first reads endpoint-scoped Redeven product settings.

Canonical deletion runs before product cleanup.

Flower sends `force=true` after destructive confirmation, retires the local cache entry only after HTTP success, and has no pending, committed, failed, operation-id, or durable-intent UI state.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Redeven never stores a fork saga, source/destination turn or run identity mapping, Floret fork result, canonical title, or Agent lifecycle snapshot. Product adoption cannot authorize a foreign source, choose a different destination, reconstruct canonical content, or compensate by deleting a valid Floret destination.

Redeven never opens or edits Floret tables, never restores a deleted canonical thread, never reports asynchronous deletion progress, and never fabricates an atomic transaction across the two owners. Retry convergence is based only on typed Floret deletion/not-found errors and the current Redeven catalog row, not error text, polling, or a recovery projection.

concepts.title: Flower canonical thread queries
concepts.summary:
Flower exposes two read-only tools for finding another readable conversation
and reading its content: `thread_query` and `thread_read`. The tool contract
is intentionally smaller than Floret's published general query API.
`threads.aggregate` is not registered or dispatched.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Find, browse, read

- `thread_query` defaults to `object: threads`, listing recently updated
  conversations first. Optional `title` is one literal, case-insensitive title
  fragment. Optional `thread_id` selects one exact conversation.
- To browse `messages` or `tool_calls`, provide one `thread_id`. Records are
  chronological; there are no model-controlled sort keys or detailed filters.
- `limit` defaults to 50, with a maximum of 200. Continue with `next_cursor` and
  unchanged input. Pass a record's `ref` to `thread_read` for complete content,
  following its cursor until no continuation remains.
- Nested `filter`, message-body matching, argument/result matching, keywords,
  phrases, time/role/tool/status predicates, grouping and aggregation are not
  accepted by the tool schema or handler. Unsupported inputs fail explicitly.
- Reasoning, secrets and private provider state remain excluded. Tool arguments
  and confirmed results are available only through authorized content reads.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Authorization owner

Authenticated session authority supplies read permission, user, endpoint and
namespace identity. Redeven reconstructs the readable scope for every page and
read. Tool parameters and returned references never grant authority. Changed
scope invalidates frozen cursors; a new query starts under current permission.
The adapter uses published Floret public APIs and never reads Floret SQL or
reconstructs canonical records.

## Historical results and presentation

Saved query/read results remain previewable after restart and after their
original refs expire. The historical aggregate result renderer remains solely
for immutable already-saved tool exchanges; it cannot dispatch aggregation.
Private query contents are not added to Activity snapshots. The intent label
and explicitly opened, bounded result preview remain the presentation boundary.

## Storage and execution

The canonical owner stores source locators and metadata. Flower requires no
full-text index and schedules no startup or background indexing. Metadata-only
browsing requests one thread's ordered records; canonical full content is read
only as needed. Floret's retired optional indexing declarations are not a
product capability. The engine's published query API may retain compatibility
filters without exposing those filters to Flower's model tools.

concepts.title: Direct image reading and tool media retention

frontmatter.title: Direct image reading and tool media retention

concepts.summary:
image_read inspects authorized files/snapshots. File references stay references; results use native
images, not browsers, temporary servers or Base64 result JSON. One in-process media gate protects writes and the complete canonical inventory through deletion, following Floret's published retention contract.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- File mode accepts file_path and optional target_id; locator mode requires a
  canonical media:v1 locator, excludes file_path/target_id, and reuses original
  bytes without reopening the source. Default behavior remains unchanged.
- Every permission mode checks image capability, CanRead, filesystem scope and
  ToolTargetPolicy. Unavailable explicit targets fail without device fallback.
- File reads and crop results retain their 10 MiB bound; Computer snapshots retain
  16 MiB. All reads are bounded to 16384 pixels per side and 32 megapixels. Tool
  guidance discloses these limits and the width/height/size_bytes result fields.
- Locator-only crop accepts integer x/y/width/height within original image pixels,
  never clips, and saves a new lossless PNG with source_crop metadata. It uses
  fresh canonical authorization. Image pixels differ from CSS action coordinates.
- image_read stores original snapshots, while every model input (including crops
  and summaries) uses [default model preparation](computer-use-media.md). Original
  locators remain available for detail crops; no durable derivative cache exists.
- Floret preserves every image in ordered summary batches; capacity failures shrink
  the same unconsumed batch. Current user images remain exact. Tokens and JSON bytes have separate
  limits; indivisible overflow fails.
- Switching to a text model preserves all images and presents verified metadata and
  locators through the [attachment manifest](flower-attachment-resources.md), without
  blocking selection or claiming that the model has seen pixels.
- toolMediaStore retains immutable images in computer/keyframes across source
  changes, Retry, restart, Fork and compaction.
- Previews check ownership/canonical membership directly. Markdown images stay unchanged.

## Maintenance and interactive writes

Maintenance
skips a held gate or queued writers. An interactive write cancels a running
maintenance scan and waits for that scan to settle; its own wait honors caller
cancellation. Partial or failed inventory never authorizes deletion. No second
membership ledger, detached scan, speculative unlock or input replay is used.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: No storage migration, Floret-table queries or second media-membership ledger.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Configuration and protocol
Standalone configuration lives at `<stateDir>/ai/mcp.json`, with schema version 2, one monotonic configuration revision, and server revisions for optimistic edits. Persistence failure leaves the in-memory catalog unchanged.

Catalog limits are 32 servers, 128 tools per server, 32 KiB per schema, and 4 MiB total persisted configuration.

They cannot be edited through standalone MCP writes.

## Standalone identity
Creation accepts an omitted local ID and display name. The runtime generates a cryptographically random lowercase ID with an mcp_ prefix, independently of the name or connection address; duplicate explicit IDs are conflicts, never replacements. Edits require the saved ID and revision. Missing IDs with a nonzero revision fail without creating another connection. Existing IDs and exact-ID Skill dependency matching remain unchanged.

For new unnamed connections, use the HTTP hostname or local executable basename, then prefer serverInfo.title followed by serverInfo.name from the existing successful initialize exchange. Automatically selected names are trimmed, limited to 120 UTF-8 bytes without splitting a character, and reject control characters. Explicit names win. Edits with an omitted name retain the saved name, and checks never rename a connection. Disabled creation uses connection-derived names without starting a command or contacting the server.

Typing or opening a form does not probe connections. Failed discovery/persistence does not create a saved identity; retry remains an explicit user action. The persisted schema and credential-preservation rules do not change.

## Presentation icons
Save and explicit Check read `serverInfo.icons` from the existing SDK initialize result. Connection-preserving disabled edits retain icons; changed connection settings clear stale discovery.

Rejected sources receive the generated identity described in [the shared UI contract](../ui/flower-extensions.md#navigation).

## Execution and dependencies
Enabled, previously discovered tools join the dynamic tool surface before the existing permission filter. Their identity binds the exact server configuration and tool schema, so a changed or disabled configuration cannot execute through an old invocation name.

Enabled, checked configuration satisfies the catalog indicator; it does not promise current network reachability or bypass approval.

## Image results
Typed ImageContent and image EmbeddedResource blobs become immutable tool-media
attachments before the text display limit. Ordered text placeholders retain each
image's attachment index, original dimensions and canonical locator. Arbitrary
strings, structured JSON and resource links never trigger image downloads.
Admission bounds each original to 10 MiB/32 megapixels and each result to 64
images/32 MiB; HTTP SSE events allow 48 MiB for Base64 and metadata. The released SDK
retains its 16 MiB stdio frame bound; transport rejection is explicit and never
authorizes replay. Provider delivery uses the shared [model policy](computer-use-media.md).
If image retention fails after CallTool returned, the result records confirmed
invocation completion and unavailable output. This does not authorize tool replay,
including when retention observes cancellation. Already retained attachments stay
paired with the completed result.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
MCP tools are conservatively mutating and open-world regardless of server annotation claims. An MCP handler cannot run directly without that proof.

Server tool errors and known connection failures remain distinct from an unknown execution outcome.

Redeven passes model output capability as Floret ModelMaxOutputTokens, and only an explicit per-request limit as MaxOutputTokens. It never maps capability to a fixed output reservation.

## Mechanism
Model reasoning capability, stream fields, history replay, and immutable thread settings are governed by [model reasoning capabilities and transport](model-reasoning-runtime.md#runtime-capability).

Unsupported transports reject non-empty state before HTTP.

Hosted-turn diagnostics record the selected wire mode, and Floret lifecycle audit events carry batch index, batch size, event type, and observation time so operators can distinguish model serialization, provider single-call output, approval wait, dispatch, and completion without feeding diagnostics back into scheduling.

## Prompt and repository rule sources

## Related provider history
Provider-visible history, render lineage, and unavailable-tool continuity are owned by [Model provider surface and history](model-provider-surface-and-history.md).

## Related context usage
Usage accounting, context pressure, compaction, token budgets, and capacity failures are owned by [Model context usage and compaction](model-context-usage-and-compaction.md#usage-and-recovery).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Usage and recovery
### Evidence and projection
Retain frozen trigger candidates, pressure and validated replacement. Install complete actor-owned context before version publication. Changed context bypasses text cadence; equal snapshots coalesce bounded text. Host never accumulates usage, reconstructs lifecycle, invents budgets or infers capacity from weights.

### Independent capacity evidence
Published request-byte/image evidence is independent of token pressure. Preparation failures retain actual/limit bytes; HTTP413 invents no counts. Keep last confirmed token ratio even if low and explain the separate capacity cause/message-text estimate. Cause-only events, reload and Desktop RPC preserve this distinction; absent historical evidence is unknown, without error-text inference.

RPC reconstructs upstream typed cause before Engine recovery; version handshake rejects incompatible peers. Localized inline image-history organizing divider shows measured details. Floret owns bounded ordered image-summary batches, protected current inputs, replacement validation and schema34 migration. Failed/canceled summaries install no partial checkpoint; completed tools never replay.

### Timeline
One compact row/short separators and surface-owned tooltip, no expansion/reflow. Success explicitly labels message-text estimates, not full request input. Localize absent/running/canceled counts; wrap original errors and localize only missing fallback. Tooltip follows surface/global theme, prefers above unless bounded, permits hover/selection through delayed pointer exit, and dismisses on Escape/Tab/blur/outside/process collapse. Retain touch/keyboard and independent Retry.

## Request measurement
Pressure uses qualified native prefix plus remaining frozen estimate, or full estimate without matching proof. Desktop prepares on credential owner, returning estimate/fingerprint; execution/refits/retries share frozen input. DeepSeek uses upstream credential-scoped expiring authorized image uploads across preparations. RPC claims native proof only if transferred and validated.

Logical preparation context owns Desktop handles through settlement/discard; closing one attempt retains replay while context lives. Published Floret v7.107.4 validates saved DeepSeek assistant boundaries within Runtime-grouped messages when Retry adds a tool after reasoning. Forward opaque state unchanged; restart/Fork retain effects/history without replay.

One-part request credit, bounded response reassembly and per-request cancellation isolate slow consumers. Handle ownership transfers only on client acknowledgement; earlier cancellation releases Desktop resources. Old peers fail handshake. Upstream owns90% threshold/output reservation. Unknown gateways, hosted execution, automatic truncation and hidden continuation provide no measurement proof. Failed/canceled attempts provide no committed response evidence.

## Manual compaction
Pure compact stops after install/noop. Goal continuation prepares context under existing Engine/current review in the same execution; upstream owns Stop/Retry/restart.

### Explicit manual intent
POST /_redeven_proxy/api/ai/threads/{id}/context/compact accepts storage_generation/client_request_id/optional continue_goal. True becomes goal_continuation only when admission finds an active canonical Goal. Failure/noop retains actionable result.

[Qualification](../operations/flower-compaction-qualification.md#compaction) owns isolated checks.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Cloud uses its catalog protocol without dispatch-time discovery.

Explicit endpoint limits, modalities, tool declarations and reasoning efforts
survive atomic snapshots and restart. Field provenance separates endpoint facts
from inherited reviewed defaults, so old snapshots still refresh shipped defaults
and partial declarations override only reported fields. Full unknown wire IDs
remain intact; complete serving facts enable only explicitly selected models. A reasoning boolean never invents effort controls; advertised Ultra remains
capability-gated. Conflicting metadata rejects the complete refresh and preserves
the previous snapshot. ChatGPT, Google, Ollama and OpenRouter retain their own
inventory contracts.

Settings retain sparse user overrides, show unknown input capabilities, expose
the usable input budget and warn when a window override exceeds the endpoint's
reported limit. Reset restores endpoint facts. Refresh never silently changes
saved selection or manual settings.

Profiles separate selection, overrides, custom definitions and default identity from metadata; visibility changes none of selection, identity, capabilities or routing.

Flower groups icon/name rows by provider: inline title/search/close, icon tiles, selection outline/check and fixed footer. Desktop: viewport-bounded 17rem width, 20rem height cap, 24px minimum rows, 10px labels and 9px provider headings. Touch: 44px targets, 16px search. Preserve search, aliases, keyboard control, refresh and management. Hide limits, image/search capabilities, quantization and alias descriptions. Unavailable rows show brief status with tooltip/accessibility reasons. Attachment feedback requires checks or attention. Long names/headings truncate with tooltips; scroll vertically.

The shared Flower UI owns provider brand rendering in Desktop and Env App. Settings, provider dialogs and model selectors use unchanged, pinned theSVG assets recorded in assets/flower_provider_icons.json; checksums and licenses are verified by the third-party notice generator. Monochrome marks use the foreground color through an alpha mask, while color marks retain their original SVG bytes. Both Kimi connection types share Kimi; the legacy chatglm type displays Z.ai; custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints use the OpenAI protocol mark without asserting endpoint ownership. No host-specific SVG paths or runtime CDN requests are used.

Both `GET /api/ai/models` modes share unfiltered `provider_catalogs` and backend `provider_defaults`: capabilities, never account availability, even before setup. Settings/drafts remain editable without usable models.

A selected platform whose catalog is unavailable shows the localized model-check failure and recovery action, never the first-use setup welcome. Preserve draft and selection; explicit model-menu refresh recovers from an authoritative directory response.

`LoadForStartup` freezes supported legacy selections before service start; no discovery wait or current-profile migration.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Tool argument ownership
Floret owns syntax/schema validation and bounded correction. Gateway and Desktop model-source RPC v7 retain exact nonempty args_json, including malformed/non-object JSON; v6 peers are fenced before streaming. Object adapters retain args; dual authorities fail. Missing identity/arguments and incomplete streams are transport failures. Canonical rejection/feedback crosses history unchanged, without host repair or correction Activity. Only validated calls acquire execution/authorization/questions. Exhaustion preserves confirmed effects and offers explicit Retry.

## Tool names
[Tool permissions](tool-permission-runtime.md) owns canonical names and the final provider surface. Definitions, calls, execution, history and Flower use the same provider-safe names; no provider alias table or prompt/script rewriting. Historical name migration belongs to its released owner, not an execution-time fallback.

## Responses
Strict OpenAI schemas make optional properties required/nullable and explicitly document null-as-omission. Restore only adapter-added nulls; canonical null/required fields and false/zero/empty remain meaningful. Canonical schemas/non-strict DeepSeek remain unchanged.

Completed reasoning ciphertext wins; matching terminal items fill only missing/null/empty. Search done bytes win when only valid action.sources differ; never merge lists. Answer annotations are independent. Validate terminal-only fallback and retain ordered done events when terminal omits them. Duplicate done, identity/content/arguments/status/input/unknown-field/missing-item/byte violations remain strict.

Map opaque SDK bytes and typed errors. CompleteWithDiagnostics exposes safe paths/boundary/counts/authority, never queries/URLs/values. Localized post-response.completed errors retain copyable safe conflict detail. Attempt epochs identify requests, not failed retries; validation cannot advance history/replay effects/change retry policy.

Floret PrepareResponsesHistory owns OpenAI/compatible/Qwen/ChatGPT replay. Hosted receipts, encrypted reasoning and functions survive disabled tools/search. Confirmed incomplete Responses retain length-continuation snapshots; failed/interrupted streams install none. ChatGPT rejects incomplete; filtering never advances history. Activity is not replay state.

Measure full native input. Only explicit API-key OpenAI responses_continuation plus Engine permission enables response-ID/suffix; others use full input. Freeze request/choice across transport retries. Rejected IDs cannot drop evidence; explicit config may force full replay. ChatGPT retains namespace/OAuth/WebSocket/published state. Historical ID-only states remain opt-in but missing bytes are unrecoverable; new state stores full upstream envelopes. Reader removal needs a future-major migration. Prefix changes discard stale IDs/suffix; upstream isolates model/account/secrets. Manual Retry/Fork preserve facts/tools and clear source state.

CommitAssistant binds full text once before ordered functions. Old split bindings remain readable at saved prefixes; remap only native-proven whitespace coordinates and save on next successful commit. Preserve search/reasoning/phases; changed role/content/tool/namespace/order fails without reset/replay. ResponsesHistoryError exposes safe reason, zero-based record/canonical positions, counts and allowlisted fields through history_detail/Desktop RPC. Both hosts distinguish pre-network preparation from post-response commit and show details/manual Retry without unrelated setup.

Append-only lineage keys provider/model/reasoning/prompt/local-hosted tools/adapter/context policy/state compatibility. Flower uses saved Activity or neutral display, never unknown JSON/arguments.

## Measurement/recovery
Floret EstimateRenderedRequest owns provider rendering/signatures and vocabulary-backed counts; unknown models use an explicit multilingual BPE proxy. Server rendering may differ; no host calibration/preflight. [Measurement](model-context-usage-and-compaction.md#request-measurement) owns frozen-prefix pressure/accounting; [recovery](model-request-recovery.md) owns retries/deadlines/diagnostics.

## Anthropic
Published Floret owns HTTP/SSE, frozen cache hints, authorized attachments and signed output; Redeven maps public content/controls/usage/events. Brand implies no behavior. Engine allows at most four ephemeral cache markers, separate from opaque state. Cache-off retains signed history; secret changes clear reuse.

Completed output survives continuation/restart. Retry/Fork/compaction retain facts and clear source without invented thinking/answer conversion. Frozen retries resolve no attachments and use new attempt IDs. Usage separates uncached/read/write; measured input requires complete partitions and no transformed hosted/signed input, otherwise estimate. Failed streams preserve billing without history advance. Structured HTTP errors/exact limits remain diagnostic.

## DeepSeek temporary images
Published Floret owns upload/validation/expiring reuse/accounting/frozen replay. Explicit official HTTPS root (/v1 allowed): one-hour expiry, 48MiB request. Custom endpoints remain inline/32MiB. Runtime/Desktop independently scope reuse by provider identity; endpoint/credential changes select a new owner. Rotation uses HMAC-SHA256 with random local key, never reusable plain credential hashes. Reauthorize each preparation; no host file-ID persistence/migration. Explicit missing/expired references permit one upstream re-preparation; quota/upload/media errors never enter summary loops.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Runtime capability
### Capability and transport
OpenAI-compatible Chat reasoning is capability-driven. Redeven reads only response fields named by that result, emits their fragments as reasoning without trimming provider whitespace, and never treats reasoning-only output as assistant body text.

Budget-only and fixed-thinking models never acquire synthetic effort names or a toggle merely because another model supports one.

### Default selection
Default asks for the model's own reasoning behavior. Thread creation, Thread
edits, and every Turn canonicalize it once, in
`config.CanonicalAIReasoningSelection`: on a model without verified reasoning
controls a budget-free Default is the omitted selection and is neither stored
nor sent. Default with a budget, Off, On, and named efforts remain explicit
intent and are rejected for such a model; personal memory keeps no reasoning
choice for it. Clients may send Default without knowing the model's capability
and must not drop or rewrite it themselves.

### Settings ownership
Thread model, reasoning and permission settings are Redeven product state. Execution authority records admission permission for historical attribution only, never as live tool authorization. The configured `current_model_id` initializes future threads only.

### Automatic titles
Published Floret v7.26.0 owns title reasoning and output limits. They never change the thread's saved reasoning choice or the main response policy.

The [live timeline contract](../ui/flower-live-timeline.md) owns canonical title status, persistence, and workspace-summary presentation.

## Selection controls
Loading, reconnecting and rendering never write reasoning preferences. Explicit new-thread Off survives shared remounts/attachment preparation; a confirmed non-reasoning model clears unsupported draft intent.

One localized ordered option list serves all controls; explicit Default remains distinct.

| Capability | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean | Default, supported Off, On |
| Named efforts | Default, supported Off, declared levels only |
| Token budget | Bounded input; clearing removes override |
| Fixed thinking | Noninteractive Always on |
| Unknown thinking controls | Noninteractive Model controlled with explanation |
| No reasoning | No control |

sections.body:

This is shared Redeven UI policy, not a Floret API or a second preference store. Runtime continuation uses the [immutable Turn surface](floret-thread-runtime.md); no reasoning override is added to an input answer.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Adapters supply HTTP/stream/close-code facts; Engine owns bounded replay, cancellation, attempt identity and draft retirement.

Redeven neither repairs old cancellation records nor owns a second retry loop.

Classification does not
change retry advice, cancellation, response validation or tool dispatch. Original error messages and wrapped causes are retained separately from the
sanitized summary. Published Floret v7.101.0 owns the FailureDetails contract. The authorized original field preserves complete HTTP/SSE bytes, messages,
status and native identifiers without truncation, normalization or redaction. Bytes remain base64 in JSON; valid UTF-8 also has a readable original_body_text
view. Partial reads retain received bytes and explicitly mark incompleteness. Request headers, keys and prompts are not collected. Returned evidence may
contain private provider content and must be rendered as literal text.

The Responses attempt collector normalizes failures before attaching transport
facts. Its versioned envelope preserves HTTP status, request/response identifiers,
terminal event, output index when known, and Floret attempt identity through
Desktop RPC and canonical failure storage. Logs serialize numeric timings and
only the safe failure classification, excluding original evidence. Restart retains the details without
replaying the request; older envelopes remain readable. Flower shows the safe
reason with collapsed, expandable and fully copyable original evidence. Display
and copy preserve whitespace; provider text is never interpreted as markup. Missing historical evidence is not
reconstructed.

Tool repetition diagnostics use only validated Floret ToolRepetition fields:
tool name, call ID, consecutive count, limit, prior feedback and non-execution.
They share the existing expandable/copyable error detail with canonical thread,
turn and run identity. No argument values are exposed. Historical failures retain
their safe reason without invented counts or claims that recovery feedback was
sent. Localized copy preserves saved-result and explicit-retry guidance.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Adapters cannot broaden it.

Full input always owns estimates and fingerprints.

Official OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions requests use a deterministic,
URL-safe prompt cache key bounded to 64 ASCII characters. Redeven derives it
from Floret's namespace and the provider, normalized endpoint and account
identity without sending those values in plaintext. Disabled reuse and
non-official endpoints do not receive this key. A key-format change creates a
new provider cache namespace; it does not change canonical conversation state.

## Responses continuation configuration
`config.AIProvider.EffectiveResponsesContinuation` is the sole provider-level decision. Complete canonical input remains available when the ID is omitted.

No gateway-specific retry or alternative history owner is introduced.

## Cache usage presentation
The existing context tooltip shows the latest completed request and cumulative session cache hit rates. Recent counters project Floret's canonical confirmed usage directly and clear with its existing model/compaction boundaries. Historical cumulative usage is neither rewritten nor backfilled.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
HTTP and WebSocket use one Responses event consumer and send at most one generation per attempt. Unsupported upgrade, recoverable connection failure, interrupted streams, missing completion and precise pre-output stale continuation return to the Engine's existing budget and backoff.

There is no persistent transport history or second retry owner.

OpenAI request settings, continuation state, and input prefixes use SHA-256 only
as equality fingerprints for in-memory reuse decisions. These digests do not
store or verify user passwords and grant no authentication authority. Credential
rotation separately invalidates the live connection before another request.

concepts.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
`build_assets.sh` invokes `build_okf_bundle.sh`, which runs `cmd/okf-bundle` against explicit source and dist roots. The builder emits the bundle, manifest and checksum deterministically. Summary, contract, boundary and complete Evidence bodies are embedded as structured sections. Explicit Evidence opening returns bounded narrative text plus structured references; default Summary opening omits them. Authored source budgets still count every section; the contract/body budget excludes observational Evidence. `okf/dist/*` is generated from source and is never an authoring surface.

## Quality gates
Report mode exposes layout, indexing, summary, evidence, duplication, lifecycle and budget issues without blocking cleanup. Strict mode fails structural and source-integrity violations, overdue reviews, and source totals above the hard cap. Final integration runs strict content quality after source integrity and before verifying the generated bundle.

## Source budget
Count Unicode characters in every source Markdown file under `okf/`, including the index and log, after CRLF-to-LF normalization; exclude `okf/dist/`. The report shows total, remaining capacity and index/concept/log usage. Exceeding 900,000 warns; strict quality accepts exactly 1,000,000 and fails above it. A per-concept `quality_exception` cannot waive this hard cap.

## Review and log lifecycle
Every concept declares `lifecycle` and `reviewed_at`: review contracts every 180 days, active measurements and operational evidence every 90 days, and retained history every 365 days. Retained history also needs a concise `retention_reason`. Report mode warns and strict mode fails on invalid or overdue metadata; expiry prompts review and never deletes a document automatically. Keep `log.md` to compact summaries from the last 30 days after durable knowledge moves into its concept.

## Index and retention
Keep categories and concept links in the index; the parser derives each retrieval summary from the concept's `# Summary`. Prefer an existing concept, preserve only decision-relevant historical conclusions and counterevidence, and remove obsolete detail from the current tree so Git history remains the recovery path.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The bundle remains auditable only while OKF Markdown concepts are the sole authoring surface, source and lifecycle budgets are enforced through the shared parser, and `okf/dist/*` stays a generated verification artifact set rather than hand-edited truth. A `quality_exception` may document a justified per-concept length exception, but it never waives the source cap or other quality checks.

concepts.title: OKF tool suite
concepts.summary: Redeven exposes the embedded OKF bundle through read-only `okf_get_index`, `okf_search`, and `okf_open` builtin tools. Redeven projects bounded safe results into Floret v7.26.0 structured Activity rows, and the shared Flower surface expands those rows without reading raw OKF result JSON.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
Runtime OKF code loads the embedded bundle once, indexes root directory sections, scores structured summaries and sections in memory, and opens a concept summary or one selected section by id or path. Internal ids, paths, and unfiltered result objects never enter that display contract. OKF activity labels and operation values come from `ToolPresentationSpec`, so the Floret projection does not own a separate OKF display vocabulary.

## Tool workflow
`okf_get_index` browses `okf/index.md` as a structured directory and returns summaries plus section counts. `okf_search` returns a bounded short candidate list with query-aware snippets and the best matching section id/title; title and Summary matches outrank section body matches.

Evidence narrative participates in search and the section catalog. Explicit `section: "evidence"` reads its bounded body and references; `include_evidence` on another section adds only structured references. Default opening omits evidence content.

Models should follow `okf_get_index -> okf_search -> okf_open Summary -> okf_open section` and must not rely on snippets for detailed contracts.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The tools return scoped Redeven repository knowledge and do not mutate OKF source or dist artifacts. They must not be used for current news, recent public events, market or pricing facts, third-party documentation, external facts, or general web facts. Source-level conclusions still require file or terminal verification after OKF navigation.

concepts.title: Provider configuration validation
concepts.summary: Redeven owns configuration, credentials and Flower readiness across every settings entrypoint and provider-bundle save. Floret's public runtime contract is unchanged. Invalid saves preserve configuration and credentials; authentication/network failures remain execution errors.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Readiness and saving
All settings entrypoints and provider-bundle saves enforce the same completeness rules. Readiness reflects actual stored secrets and selected catalog membership. Ollama and custom compatible endpoints may run without a key. Unknown discovered models need complete endpoint declarations or explicit capability configuration.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| API key | Required for local providers except Ollama/custom compatible. Desktop and Redeven AI sources retain separate session authority. |
| Base URL | Optional adapter default for OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini; explicit HTTP(S) otherwise. |
| Display name | Optional; derive from provider type/identity. |
| Models | Explicit named list or selected_models, including empty selection. Legacy exclusion profiles require review. Preserve unavailable selections without inventing capacity. |
| Limits | Published defaults may supply omitted limits. Explicit compatible/OpenRouter/xAI/Groq/Ollama models and custom catalog entries require context. Unknown discoveries require context, output and tools capability; reviewed models retain optional output limits. |
| Brave key | New or stored key required when Brave search is enabled. |

## Kimi Code
The kimi_code provider uses its own subscription key and official China/global coding endpoint. Admit only six reviewed model/wire identities, capacity ceilings and reasoning levels. An explicit 1M override is user intent, not entitlement evidence. Preparation rejects unknown IDs, thinking-off and response-ID continuation before dispatch.

concepts.title: Flower child runtime and parent event boundary

frontmatter.title: Flower child runtime and parent event boundary

concepts.summary: Floret owns canonical child threads, reports and parent events. Its flat provider schema requires spawn(task_name,task_description,message), send_input(target,message), close(target) and wait(ids); status/inspect deduplicate target then ids.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Child runtime
subagent_manage supports spawn, send_input, wait, list, status, inspect, close and close_all. Reject non-null fields from other actions, including empty filters, before resources/authorization; strict-provider null means omission. The same pure action decoder owns bounded model correction in published Floret v7.107.9. Rejected calls are not actionable Activity; valid values stay unchanged. Child scope, stale targets, storage and permission checks remain execution checks, never correction or replay authority.

send_input steers active work or starts an idle turn, including after completion/cancellation. close cancels one child; close_all covers unfinished direct children across parent turns under current_thread (default). Reject current_run and list/target filters. Neither deletes history nor includes descendants.

Returned canonical views distinguish admitted cancellation (accepted/accepted_count for exact thread/turn/run) from settled stopped/closed counts. Already-terminal children do not count. affected_ids contains confirmed admissions; each child's state/failure, including unknown effects, stays authoritative. Batch failure retains confirmed siblings, unconfirmed_ids and unattempted_ids. A committed effect with failed projection returns non-retryable uncertainty; Activity marks the failed target unknown. Inspect before another action; no replay or second lifecycle store. Model results retain all candidates; Activity caps targets at 200 with explicit truncation and full requested count.

Model results keep child identity/name/status/current turn/queue count/failure/interactions, excluding display timestamps, duplicate IDs/counts and UI flags. Spawn/wait omit repeated descriptions; list/inspect retain them. Omit preview only when complete handoff is included. Complete handoffs bypass generic caps; explicit event reads preserve full pages. Bounded-wait metadata uses original execution results, not compact projection. Descriptions define semantics without prescribing coordination.

wait attention_required carries canonical input/approval counts without a second parent confirmation. Requests remain blocked at the child's own authority boundary; parent may use completed handoffs, do independent work or explicitly ask about dependencies. Unchanged attention is neither timeout nor progress. Parent UI uses its canonical lifecycle; child badges retain real requests. Persisted parent requests remain operable after restart.

### Child ownership and historical references
Forks copy conversation facts, not child ownership. Missing targets are missing, never completed/timed out.

## Parent events
Published subagent_read_events reads only events addressed to the current parent, including earlier turns. Floret atomically records canonical completion, failure, cancellation, interruption, normalized timeout and input/approval attention references. Browser state is temporary reading/disclosure only.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Labels/previews are not identity/results. Redeven never queries Floret storage, persists child lifecycle/handoffs, infers membership from Activity or adds publication, permission-snapshot, recovery, receipt, budget or authority-barrier state. Events are context observations, not another result store or scheduler. Original message owns task/execution authorization.

concepts.title: AI terminal tool runtime
concepts.summary: Redeven owns PTYs and bounded output; Floret v7 owns canonical tool calls, interactions, effect attempts, results and Activity. [Task-file placement](flower-task-files.md) supplies thread scratch/staging through child-only environment variables while preserving project cwd and OS temporary path conventions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Cleanup waits for owned processes to be reaped. PTYs use Floret execution/effect
identities. `terminal_exec` defaults to a 5-second initial wait (omitted/zero
`yield_ms`); positive waits cap at 30 seconds. Yield returns a live process ID,
not termination. Commands have a disclosed 30-minute lifetime. Terminate/Service
shutdown stop owned processes; cancellation during initial exec wait stops the
command, while later read cancellation preserves it.

Simple text/rule reads and discovery use shared [file tools](tool-permission-runtime.md#file-inspection).
Shell remains available for pipelines/specialized formats; browser previews use
managed discover/select/exec. Guidance never changes ownership or permission.

`cwd` is preferred; `workdir` is equivalent. Both empty use run cwd; relative paths
resolve there. Two nonempty fields must resolve to the same authorized directory,
including symlinks. Neither wins. Conflict returns `INVALID_PATH`,
`reason=conflicting_working_directories`, `process_started=false` before admission
or process creation.

On macOS/Linux, one exit worker observes without reaping, kills the process group,
retires numeric signaling, verifies no members within 2 seconds, then reaps/drains.
The unreaped root pins PID through cleanup. Child cleanup preserves shell exit
codes; only confirmed Stop means cancellation. Stop/input failure/30-minute limit/
shutdown share this worker. Unconfirmed cleanup reports runtime error and retains
workload admission; settlement stops the watchdog. Foreground processes use their
returned ID. Backgrounding/nohup cannot transfer ownership; escaping PTY group or
session is unsupported. Independent services need managed lifecycle. Names, CPU
and age never prove ownership.

`terminal_read` returns bounded incremental output after `after_seq`, up to 60
seconds or earlier on output/exit. Normal expiry reports `wait_expired`/`wait_ms`
and retains ID/cursor; `timed_out` means command timeout. Continue with returned
`last_seq`, without sleeps/restarts. Published Floret BoundedWait measures handler
time and owns repeat protection; immediate/failed/canceled/early reads and nearby
effects get no exemption. No extra retry counters, clocks, wakes or durable ledger.

Read cancellation preserves process/cursor and confirms cancellation after
observation returns. Execution/input retain uncertain-effect rules. `terminal_write`
bounds stdin; terminate kills the group and waits for reap/drain. Thread Stop owns
cleanup policy. Model output carries output/status/cursor/wait/exit facts, without
repeating command/cwd/timing from canonical Activity. Browser payloads exclude
local paths, stdin, authorization proofs and effect internals.

Completion Activity previews whole UTF-8 chunks within 8,000 bytes. Full retained
chunks seal independently; preview truncation/watermarks describe only shown bytes.
Completion omits invocation-owned command/cwd. Persistence failures log bounded
identities immediately and remain shutdown errors, never trigger replay.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
No authority barriers, admission receipts, recovery handles or projection-cursor
waits. Reads never retry settlement. Detail polling refreshes bytes, never canonical
status or provider dispatch.

concepts.title: Tessiven Flower tools and scoped Runtime operations

frontmatter.title: Tessiven Flower tools and scoped Runtime operations

concepts.summary: Flower maps authorized code, configuration and Runtime facts into canvas versions. For tessiven_manage_instance, open prepares and returns entrance information for the running bound service and may run its preparation hook. It does not launch a browser or start a stopped service.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Conversation scope

Tessiven tools and `redeven-tessiven` guidance are available only to canvas-owned
conversations and their child executions. Ordinary and plugin-creation turns do
not advertise or activate them, even while the Tessiven service is running.
A canvas reference alone never enables this tool surface. The product supplies
the scoped registry and managed context through published Floret APIs; no engine
API, dependency replacement, or canonical journal migration is required.

New turns and new Goals carry `create.tessiven_canvas_id` (or the Goal's
`new_thread` field). Redeven validates the canvas and records ownership before
publishing root settings or starting a provider request. Create retries retain
ownership; an existing ordinary root cannot be adopted. Each canvas retains many
conversations and one active root in `flower_thread_id`. New creates, new Goals
and explicit forks activate their resulting conversation only while the previous
root and its descendants are idle, without pending input, approval, queue or
noninherited bound host work. Explicit selection uses the same check. Clients
cannot activate a child as another root.

A canvas-scoped, cancellation-aware in-process gate orders activation with send,
retry, Goal submission, compaction, interaction responses and queued/child input
admission. The execution factory checks the same root identity for automatic
continuation and restart, including prebuilt child agents. Inactive attempts fail
before provider dispatch. Lifecycle facts remain exclusively in Floret; no
parallel run ledger or domain migration is introduced. Busy activation and
inactive execution are explicit HTTP 409 conflicts. Save-only Goal edits do not
execute, and child threads inherit the active parent's scope.
Ordinary lists, live summary
membership, conversation queries and cross-conversation references exclude these
threads; direct authorized content reads remain available to the canvas UI.
Canonical runtime facts and tool execution stay owned by Floret.

## Runtime operations
Discovery starts no process/business session and path refs grant no authority. Identity/generation changes or revocation stop input.

### Official surface
- `tessiven_list_runtimes` / `GET /_redeven_proxy/api/tessiven/runtimes` returns independent source availability and exact target paths.
- `tessiven_inspect_runtime` / `POST .../runtimes/inspect` reads status, bounded public diagnostics, or the original Desktop operation.
- `tessiven_manage_runtime` / `POST .../runtimes/actions` requests connection or one supported `start`, `stop`, `restart`, or `update` process operation.
- `tessiven_inspect_resource/action` retain the canonical canvas version, bound instance, and resource identity checks for Managed Services and containers.

A returned operation_id can be queried through
the corresponding inspect action=operation; absence of an ID is not retry authority.

No sibling module, replacement SDK, or product lifecycle queue is introduced.

### Source authority and discovery
Desktop registers its Tessiven host through owner-authenticated private Runtime control. Web Service, CodeSpace, nested frame, unrelated-origin and worker requests cannot declare a native source.

Ambiguous references fail closed.

### Connection and business access
Explicit connect reuses saved configuration and existing connection leases.

It cannot carry claimed permission flags, an arbitrary URL, another Runtime reference, or a process-lifecycle action.

Member removal and replacement retire the transport; no local or alternate route is substituted.

### Native lifecycle handoff
Process actions use saved direct Desktop placements and the existing [Desktop lifecycle owner](../desktop/desktop-runtime-process-lifecycle.md#process-lifecycle). The model cannot choose a download URL or release version; the existing release selector owns updates and post-operation verification.

Unknown connection outcomes require checking the selected connection in its native owner rather than retrying.

## Flower document tools
- Tessiven tools read the canonical schema, list/read/validate versions, save a complete new version, inspect explicit targets, and execute one exact bound instance when the existing permission and approval checks allow it.
- Read-only inspection of a missing, non-current, or unauthorized Runtime returns structured `unavailable` state without a binding. Unknown mutation outcomes disable another mutation until the original manager has been inspected.

## Exact resources and partial inventory

`inspect`, `logs` and `operation` accept a direct resource binding without any
canvas fields or a canvas library. A manually added `port_forward` is an address
reference without a management binding; inventory and matching names cannot
establish its backing service. Canvas-backed queries retain their immutable version/instance
resolution. Managed bindings call the original manager's exact-ID `Inspect`,
not its all-service inventory. Their credential-free `service` projection
contains description, deployment, template, configured workspace, port and
current release, never settings, session URLs or credentials.

`list` returns `complete` and scoped `issues` alongside confirmed resources.
A failed manager, endpoint or container read does not erase independent results;
not-installed engines require no inventory. Unread scopes are not empty scopes.
Cancellation remains an error. Direct target failures remain explicit and never
select another resource or discover a canvas. The tool description carries this
contract at the final provider boundary.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
### UI and compatibility
The Connected environments panel and Runtime node entry use this same service. The Runtime Dialog is part of the loaded Tessiven page; opening it must not suspend the page or show its navigation loading placeholder.

Gateway v6 application access, Tessiven DSL, and persistent database lineages retain their current shapes.

Flower and the UI call the same Tessiven service; neither writes its database directly. Explicit connection uses the original native owner; missing authority never substitutes a local target. External and unmanaged resources support inspection and explanation only.
