sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Inspection and installation

GitHub repositories may expose several plugins through `.redevplugin/index.json`; the user selects a plugin before inspection. A package URL or upload uses the same inspection contract.

Review binds exact inspected bytes, intended instance/revision, owner and session. Submission uses one request ID and the released durable `StartInspectedInstall` API. A lost response queries that same request; it never invents a replacement operation. The Shell restores owner-scoped receipts, including first-install failures with no inventory row. Closing Plugin Center does not stop observation; changing the authenticated owner cancels and clears it.

Execution status and mutation outcome are distinct. A committed outcome requires inventory reconciliation even if final execution reports failure. Unknown outcomes stay read-only. A definite failure requires a fresh review; the UI never silently erases retained data, grants access, or retries uncertain effects. Installation enables the plugin while missing grants remain separate action-level authorization boundaries.

## Updates

Manual checks inspect the installed original source. GitHub provenance uses immutable repository identity, not a mutable owner/name or a market replacement. Source changes require explicit consent. Older versions use the separate downgrade lifecycle; same-version changed bytes are rejected. A market disappearance does not change installed authority.

Automatic updates are an explicit per-installation preference, off by default. While an authorized session is active, Redeven checks enabled installations after a bounded delay and at bounded intervals. It uses the same original-source inspection and durable installation path, only when the Host reports automatic eligibility: a higher version, same source and unchanged security declarations. New capabilities require manual review. Uploaded packages have no automatic remote source. No synthetic session, unattended host scheduler, or new product persistence entity is introduced.

Before automatic submission, owner-scoped durable receipts are reconciled. Pending or unknown operations prevent replay; a previous failed attempt at the same candidate requires review. Surface shutdown and inventory reconciliation use the existing placement coordinator. Neither automatic nor manual update grants permissions or overrides user-disabled state.

## Retained data and downgrade

The released Host owns target-filtered retained-data discovery, exact inspection, one-shot recovery and read-only reconciliation. Recovery binds owner, publisher/plugin, data shape, generation, management revision and active fingerprint. Atomic generation swaps preserve prior data and do not restore grants, secrets or enabled state. Discovery/inspection/status require Read; commit requires Write; disable requires Admin.

Declared data conversion runs in isolated bounded generations. Failure/cancellation preserves old bytes; committed/unknown outcomes reconcile without replay. Downgrade restores the exact historical package's retained generation. Redeven never copies opaque data, interprets converter code, or implements platform-store migrations.

Review shows concise saved-data impact and expandable verified differences. Permission grants remain independent explicit choices. No duplicate install wizard, dispatcher, package parser, or destructive retry path exists.

## Admission and ownership
`/_redeven_proxy/api/remote-desktop` is independent from application launch. Every session and forward belongs to the authenticated user; renderer-supplied identity never authorizes a route.

The same policy fences new admission under the manager lock, so an HTTP request authorized before revocation cannot recreate the removed desktop.

## Platform boundary
macOS uses the exact remote Swift package in the existing Runtime helper.

The canonical official Alpine source remains the final fallback; every download still checks the expected size and SHA-256 before atomic cache publication, and a failed archive download can move to the next trusted source.

Capability normalization also applies to a retried connection after accepting or declining takeover, so a removed display cannot return through the stored request.

## Media and office interaction
Control and media travel through separate Flowersec native proxy streams bound to the same product attachment. Cancellation retires the selection and releases held keys; lock-screen input cannot use that text path.

Native session and frame authority remain governed by this concept.

concepts.summary: Desktop owns SSH authorization/UI lifetime, Floe Native Apps privileged preparation and Runtime service authorization/audit. Only the owning root/main frame of an RWX-authorized SSH environment uses typed deployment IPC. Sensitive admin streams retain no stdout/stderr diagnostics.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- The upstream manager owns ensure/stop/uninstall and supported migrations. Unknown/future/unverifiable ownership remains unchanged. Service readiness, Runtime admission and capture readiness are separate; absent scanout cannot invalidate admitted policy.
- During component preparation, the published manager state is carried through Desktop as an optional, allowlisted `media_state` field. It is accepted only with the `preparing_media` deployment stage; byte totals remain optional and are shown only when measured. States after byte transfer describe verification, installation, validation and packaging work and therefore remain indeterminate until the manager reports readiness.
- Deployment progress separates SSH session startup, host inspection, service package creation, Runtime package preparation, per-file upload, desktop component preparation, service changes and Runtime verification. Runtime downloads and SSH uploads publish measured byte counts when available; upload file identities and transfer direction are allowlisted, and progress is throttled. Unknown totals and local verification/build work stay indeterminate; no percentage or time estimate is inferred.
- Before upload, one SSH batch checks the requested service, graphics worker, license and Runtime bytes against trusted package SHA-256 digests. The SSH identity owns a bounded four-file cache at `$HOME/.cache/redeven/desktop-transfer-v1`; entries are read-only and atomically replaced. Each hit is copied into a private transaction directory and its actual bytes are hashed there. Missing, changed, corrupt or unsafe entries are uploaded individually. Symlinked or untrusted cache directories fail closed. Inspection and publication each have a 30-second bound and accept cancellation; the UI reports inspection without fabricated byte progress or empty metrics.
- Cache reuse is a transport optimization, never proof of installation or authorization. Every connection still runs manager ownership and integrity checks, administrator authorization, actual Runtime admission, challenge/commit and rollback. Transactions clean their staging copies; fixed cache names do not accumulate prior versions.
- A kernel-authenticated root manager holds maintenance ownership. Unknown attachment counts on older services require confirmation. Stage cleanup is independently bounded; transport loss is not rollback proof.
- Linux login-screen capability failures preserve published, redacted reason codes across the native service, Runtime status and launcher. Stale compositor binaries after an OS update (`LOGIN_SESSION_STALE_RUNTIME`) and changed, missing, ambiguous, seat or TTY identities are host-action states with refresh guidance; unsupported desktops remain unsupported. concepts.title: Remote desktop viewer interaction
concepts.summary: Published input/playback and session contracts own current-frame authority. Recovery keeps controls usable; disconnect stops media/input with confirmed removal or Retry. Frozen pixels never imply connection. This desktop-only policy does not apply to host application windows, which use their own upstream cursor contract.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Lock-screen input
When a lock-screen frame is painted and acknowledged in control mode, the viewer
arms physical-only unlock input automatically. Paint and acknowledgement may
arrive in either order; both paths attempt arming, and subsequent acknowledgements
must not steal focus. The host lock screen remains unobscured, and a rate-limited
interaction explains the wait instead of claiming that authentication failed.
Opening a panel, losing the socket, changing generation or mode, and every
unpainted transition revoke the armed target. Backend frame, generation, control
owner and physical-input checks remain mandatory for every unlock event.

## Input and clipboard
The published Floe input and pointer controllers own client composition, physical keys, pointer gestures and release. Mouse and drag movement retains only the latest pending position, bounded to 120 submissions per second.

## Toolbar and window
Desktop opens an isolated owned window; browsers open a separate viewer. Ended sessions explain how to start a new connection from the launcher and never expose an ineffective Reconnect action.

The toolbar contains desktop-session controls only; it does not show a file-browser shortcut.

Explicit Disconnect closes that device; an enabled sound toggle must never hide a closed audio context after reconnect.

Compatibility epoch 35 requires both Desktop and Runtime to understand explicit reasoning `on` alongside the existing default, off, effort, and budget choices. Earlier clients reject `on`; ordinary epoch admission prevents a mixed pair from accepting a Flower or Desktop model-source request it cannot interpret. See the [reasoning selection contract](../ai/model-reasoning-runtime.md#selection-controls) for model capability and control semantics.

Epoch 59 pairs Runtime authorization requests with the shared Desktop and Env App OpenAI account picker. Epoch 71 requires truthful per-attachment Gateway connection phases and a collection-only owner status API. Durable joining/joined/removal state is separate from live controller observations. The service refreshes system metrics every two seconds and process metrics every ten seconds.

concepts.title: Runtime terminal lifecycle
concepts.summary: Floeterm owns PTY/Ghostty VT, geometry/controller epoch, input encoding, history/reset and atomic Presentation. `/_redeven_proxy/api/terminal/history-retention` is the product settings adapter: GET reads defaults or an authorized session; admin-only PUT persists and activates defaults; POST applies explicit limits to a session using its connection ID and transport generation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
The runtime wraps `termgo.NewManager` so one terminal-go `SessionActor` owns each PTY, native Ghostty VT, canonical geometry, controller epoch, input encoding, semantic history, clear/reset, and atomic Presentation.

Overflow fixtures may exceed the 8 MiB ring-buffer cap; they must recover the retained tail, preserve the stable renderer geometry after focus, and accept subsequent PTY input.

## Terminal startup and warmup
Env App hydrates one terminal session catalog after protocol connection, environment readiness, and process permission. The catalog owns canonical session metadata, notification convergence, connection epoch, permission clearing, stale-on-disconnect state, and bounded early latest values.

Diagnostics retain aggregate phase and field-presence facts only and never record session identifiers, paths, remote identity, commands, or terminal content.

## Attachment recovery presentation
The product adapter classifies explicit protocol disconnect/cancellation and published session closed/going-away/liveness/timeout errors as recoverable attachment exits. The existing bounded attachment retry preserves the terminal view and PTY identity without replaying input. Product interaction queues capture the current attachment epoch; pending input and late failures from a replaced attachment cannot affect the recovered session. Session-not-found closes the corresponding view; unclassified, rejected-stream, permission and protocol failures stay blocking and cancel pending retries. Floeterm remains the live attachment, geometry and controller owner.

## Native history budgets
Runtime persists `terminal_history_retention` with nullable `max_lines`/`max_bytes` safe nonnegative integers and applies those defaults before terminal readiness. Published terminal-go owns validation, native limit application, pruning, snapshot invalidation and atomic Presentation. Defaults affect only subsequently created sessions; existing sessions are never silently reconfigured.

Session application reuses shell/container permission and ownership checks, is principal-bound, does not transfer controller ownership, and rejects stale attachments. Limits preserve process, live screen, geometry and content epoch, while invalidating historical snapshots through the upstream history epoch. No local implementation of terminal retention or RPC retry is introduced.

Redeven coordinates its SSH bridge owner with the published acquisition source: wait for Desktop readiness before requesting local credentials and bound the product fetch/body to 15 seconds. concepts.title: Service management recovery and resource ownership

frontmatter.title: Service management recovery and resource ownership

concepts.summary: Registry owns transactions, allocations and identities; fresh backend facts govern recovery and deletion. Unknown ownership is shown honestly. Frontend code never substitutes Retry or Restart for unavailable Start. A failed Host maintenance hook may be bypassed only through an administrator's reviewed plan, and only for verified resources.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Management recovery
### Facts and actions
`ServiceFacts` separates presence, ownership, runtime state, inspection completeness, resource references, and check time.

### Review and execution
`GET /managed-web-services/{id}/inspection` requires read permission, is non-cacheable, and uses the same factual backend projection as the list.

Existing unrelated lifecycle transactions cannot be overwritten by recovery.

Instance-scoped allocation and legacy resource boundaries are owned by [Service resource ownership](#resource-ownership).

### Uninstall transaction
Uninstall uses `runtime_manifest_json`, the existing operation coordinator, and the existing event stream.

A resource recreated under the same name cannot acquire the previous deletion authorization.

Uninstall plans attribute deletion blockers to the selected resource, preserving specific inspection errors. The drawer reveals its identity and reason; retaining that resource removes only its deletion requirement. Pending reviews disable confirmation without inserting loading text or moving the footer.

Detachment remains available while it is unresolved.

### Management archives and access
Registry version 4 adds `active`, `detached`, and `uninstalled`. Only active records participate in template uniqueness and must own an authorized Forward.

Names, ports, or cached reachability never prove ownership.

## Resource ownership
### Instance allocation
New Host bindings use `instances/<service-id>/data`.

Creation must return the expected service, resource, and generation labels plus native identity.

Template permissions remain unchanged: unsupported external Compose capabilities are still rejected by template policy.

### Observation and deletion
Container ownership uses exact native ID, standard managed name, and service label.

Reference metadata exposes selected container identity, state, ports, and owning service identifiers; arbitrary engine labels and injected secrets never become public inventory fields.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The contiguous `portforward_registry_v2` 3-to-4 migration preserves bindings, configuration, private-file references, operation history, and existing resource locations. Failed migration rolls back completely; unknown versions and structural drift remain read-only failures. Desktop/Runtime compatibility epoch 15 covers these management contracts.

Existing volume names and directories are not renamed, moved, or recreated during schema upgrade. Uninstall defaults to retaining data and workspace, and cannot remove another container to satisfy a cleanup request. The [management recovery contract](#management-recovery) owns confirmation, journal resumption, archive navigation, and explicit preservation.

sections.title: Contract

## Discovery and authority
Existing `redeven-plugin-market` Worker discovers `redeven-service-template` GitHub topics; no new registry or local format. Published SDK finds root/direct `templates/<name>` documents. Default branch tracks updates; changed directory bytes require higher revision. Record confirmed unavailability, retain evidence on observation failure. Classification grants no execution trust.

Reserved interactive-desktop capabilities require all original bytes/modes to match published official manifest. Immutable metadata retains authorization across upgrades; reopening verifies digest. New privileged definitions require upstream release.

GET `/managed-web-service-templates/market-catalog` reads cache with read permission; explicit/open-discovery POST refresh requires full permission. Validate complete ordered generation, identity/presentation, redirects/regressions/pages before atomic replacement. Failure retains old evidence; environment identity fences replies. Official/community use same verified catalog and pinned flow. Discovery defaults all deployment types. Official/Community/My templates are explicit views; My templates contains accepted Git and user-authored sources. Embedded bytes only resolve legacy instances/exact runtime-profile authority, never new browsing/deployment. Preserve instance/source bindings; market refresh cannot overwrite builtins or upgrade instances.

## Acquisition and deployment
Market Deploy immediately opens configuration and acquires the owner-scoped immutable 15-minute review shared with imports. No extra review/Continue dialog. Expandable source/digest/execution evidence and required notices support final Deploy authorization. Pin numeric repository ID/commit/directory digest through Desktop transfer or Runtime acquisition; Runtime independently revalidates originals. API `source` contains repository/ref/path only; resolved identity belongs in `expected`/`snapshot.source`, rejected elsewhere.

Published v0.8.2 anonymous pinned reads use exact-commit codeload archives without REST quota. Preserve expected repository ID; validate commit metadata/every byte/mode against digest. Upstream bounds/paths/collisions/LFS/unsupported-entry rules fail closed, with no extraction/retry/API fallback/moving-ref substitution. Credentialed/unpinned reads use GitHub API with API-only request-scoped credentials and no redirects. Discovery/review/preparation saves no executable source and runs no lifecycle action.

Final install atomically commits source acceptance/binding/service/forward/receipt. Unknown admission reconciles without replay. Source/preflight/prerequisite failures remain in same drawer with explicit Retry. Existing instances/pending requests visibly block submission. Expired-source retry retains exact market identity, selected release and draft, including rejected submission. Cancel/environment change fences acquisition. Fixed buttons show busy without new loading/feedback rows; errors overlay footer. Final submit creates visible progress before receipt.

## Browsing and identity
Use published taxonomy All types/Host/Container/Docker Compose; semantic categories require upstream format, never infer from names. Active service records by exact template ID own installed/open/submission state, independent of template catalog. Stopped active records count; detached/personal copies cannot mark another template. SDK numeric repository/document namespace owns Git identity, no builtin aliases/display-name guesses. New workspaces: `<writable root>/Redeven/workspaces/managed-services/<template ID>/<instance suffix>`; retain saved paths. Preflight/final admission enforce family uniqueness across competing requests.

Search combines whitespace terms and Unicode width/case over displayed/all-localized names/descriptions, document/repository/path/default release. Source/type facets compose; counts apply source/search before type. Empty results reset to complete discovery. Refresh, including successful empty, preserves query/category/requested identity; environment fences replies. Stale/error feedback uses fixed refresh tooltip/live description under [continuity](../ui/page-loading-continuity.md), no new row. Save/import opens cleared My templates.

Separate navigation, search/actions and facets. Wrap names/categories, clamp descriptions to two lines; list/detail scroll leaves Deploy reachable. Remote details show evidence; configuration follows acquisition. Floe keyboard controls and Official/Community grouping preserve ownership. Cover four official entries without bundled duplicates, search/facets, create/import, review/admission fences, locales and 320–1440px; Runtime covers legacy lifecycle/capabilities.

concepts.title: Product storage placement and lifecycle
concepts.summary: Redeven allocates feature roots; published upstream owners retain opaque formats. Storage inspection reports bounded observations, never deletion authority or backup success. Environment data, Desktop profiles and external projects have separate ownership; relocation requires an explicit offline operation with verified recovery state.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
`StateRoot` resolves from explicit input, `REDEVEN_STATE_ROOT`, then `~/.redeven`; `StateDir` is its `local-environment` child. Desktop credentials/preferences remain in Electron userData, environment registrations in StateRoot/catalog, independent Gateway and Center in their explicitly selected roots. An Environment backup is not a Desktop profile or external-project backup.

ReDevPlugin receives only `StateDir/apps/plugins/platform`, including its control/data/assets, host adapters and author workspaces. Host migrations, SQL and recovery remain upstream. Retired root-level plugin files block plugin admission unchanged. Product draft records remain in apps/plugin-creation; market snapshots in apps/plugins. Flower Agent Plugins remain separately owned under ai/agent-plugins.

Managed skills use `apps/skills/{packages,state.json,sources.json}` in the selected Environment. Explicit `.agents/skills` remains shared user content. Managed ancestors and metadata reject symlinks/non-directory placement. Disabled/source decisions follow managed files; retired metadata blocks Flower admission. No silent HOME-based fallback imports another Environment's managed skills.

Desktop business caches all use `REDEVEN_DESKTOP_CACHE_ROOT`, or `StateRoot/cache/desktop`. userData is never a disposable cache. Existing cache acquisition, verification and eviction belong to their original owners. Old userData caches are retained; new roots reacquire verified packages without treating userData as disposable.

Config remains one atomic identity/recovery envelope: settings, binding/outbox and one-shot control artifacts cannot be split across independent writes. Provider credentials remain in secrets.json. Neither filename implies export safety. Sanitize settings exports; never export this envelope as portable preferences.

Automation allocates apps/automation. Redeven owns workflows.sqlite definitions, grants, context and artifacts; the published ReDevPlugin scheduler owns opaque schedules.sqlite. Both open before workflow admission. [Workflow ownership](automation-workflows.md) defines recovery and migrations.

Template catalog entries have no instance ID and publish no invented data path. Existing service inspection exposes actual binding-derived resource identity. New Host allocations retain instances/<service-id>/{install,data,logs}; old resource locations remain their owner's concern.

The administrator-only no-store storage endpoint inspects named Environment locations with one 20,000-entry/two-second budget, without database reads or symlink traversal outside a pinned root. Missing, unavailable and partial observations remain distinct. No global total or completeness claim is made. Settings loads the overview on authorized presentation, sorts measured locations by bytes, and shows relative usage bars, not disk-capacity percentages. One rounded group aligns owner icons, labels, observed sizes and fixed navigation actions; missing locations and path details are collapsed. Partial and unavailable observations remain explicit; no global total is inferred. It preserves last successful rows on refresh failure and aborts/fences replies when hidden or on scope/access loss. Owner links open the corresponding feature; opaque caches and coordination stores without a management surface have no invented cleanup action. Plugin Center stays independent. Flower diagnostics is a separate diagnostic category. Retired snapshot locations do not link to an obsolete restore surface. No generic recursive deletion API exists.

sections.title: Pre-release relocation
sections.body:
`scripts/relocate_prerelease_storage.py --state-dir <absolute> [--skills-source <absolute>]` previews exact moves. `--apply` requires the stopped Runtime lease; conflicts, unsupported links, special files or changed fingerprints stop without replacing data. Only relative links inside the renamed author-workspaces tree may be retained: validate every target component and link chain inside that tree without reading through links, hash each link target as opaque evidence, and preserve the original entries by renaming the tree. Absolute, escaping, missing and cyclic targets remain rejected. Other plugin trees and shared skills still reject links. SQLite and sidecars move as opaque bytes; orphan sidecars fail before migration. Shared skills copy only from the explicit source and retain originals; only Redeven-owned path metadata is rewritten. A durable journal binds original product metadata bytes to source fingerprints and permits only the selected lexical/canonical prefix rewrite; external shared-scope decisions remain separate. Explicit source arguments must match the journal. It fences feature admission until verified completion and supports interrupted moves and metadata publication. Interrupted copy stages remain untouched: inspect the reported stage, move it outside the Environment without deletion, and rerun the same command; source fingerprints are checked again. This offline tool is never called by startup and is not a permanent compatibility reader. Do not remove its guard while pending local relocations exist.

`scripts/repair_prerelease_plugin_threads.py --state-dir <absolute> --bindings <json>`
previews the one-time host thread-directory repair after a completed relocation.
Export each workspace/source binding through the released owner-bound author API.
`--apply` holds Runtime and author locks, verifies exact host database kinds and
versions, and atomically updates only matching old-to-new directory settings.
Unknown state, unrelated paths and missing bindings are rejected unchanged.
Repeated repair is a no-op; frozen launch requests, other settings and opaque
upstream stores remain untouched. Normal startup does not invoke this tool.

## Upstream format boundary
Floret v7.108.3 owns the logical-version fence for its domain-37 store and migration from recognized logical-11 state. Redeven consumes the published module with `GOWORK=off`; it does not edit upstream schema or downgrade stores. A compatible build opens retained history before readiness; an old reader must report too-new rather than label valid newer state corrupt. Build-cache deletion cannot repair this mismatch.

## Development startup

`dev_desktop.sh` performs read-only plugin placement preflight before stopping an existing Desktop or building. A blocked profile receives the exact `REDEVEN_STATE_ROOT` recovery command. `--relocate-storage` explicitly previews the selected profile, stops its Runtime, invokes the existing offline transaction and verifies placement before launch. It rejects `--no-stop` and `--stop-only`; normal launch never applies relocation. Unsupported links, conflicting targets and opaque-state validation failures remain fail closed; confined relative author-workspace dependency links follow the explicit offline rule above. A recovery flag does not authorize bypassing those checks. Preview failure leaves the running profile untouched; apply revalidates under the owner locks.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Flower recovery covers only its declared conversation/read-state/upload/media collection. Managed plugins, skills, task working files, user projects and Desktop state are not implicitly included. Existing owner-specific cleanup and recovery remain authoritative.

concepts.title: Tessiven immutable canvases, DSL and display compatibility

frontmatter.title: Tessiven immutable canvases, DSL and display compatibility

concepts.summary: Runtime owns immutable canvas YAML and contiguous version migration; clients render a frozen data-only display contract. The `tessiven_canvas_library` SQLite lineage starts at schema v1. Paths must be unique, acyclic and complete, with source validation, target validation and semantic checks.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Canvas storage
- A canvas document contains stable IDs for Runtime nodes, visual groups, business services, instances, external resources, relations, and evidence.
- Every service has at least one instance on an existing node. A missing placement fails validate/save at the service ID with a source location.
- A service kind describes its primary responsibility independently of its product name, instance role or deployment format. The [DSL versioning contract](#dsl-versions) owns version selection, read projections and write upgrades.

Canvas identities, archive state, immutable YAML versions, and idempotent request results remain intact.

The v1 → v2 → v3 library lineage preserves immutable versions and request
receipts. v3 records canvas conversation ownership in `flower_threads`, backfills
exact v2 `flower_thread_id` bindings, and retains that existing column as the
sole active conversation pointer. A thread has one canvas owner; ambiguous
historical bindings fail transactionally without mutating source state. New
conversations and forks retain every ownership row and select one active root.
Selection updates that single pointer atomically; it never deletes old journals.
Redeven serializes selection and run admission by canvas, reads canonical Floret
activity, queued work, interactions, host work and descendants before switching,
and rejects switching until the active conversation's work has settled. An idle
conversation can be reactivated without losing its history. Replayed creation
receipts never reactivate an older conversation.
Fresh, upgraded and reopened stores use the same verified schema. Floret journals
remain opaque and unchanged.

## DSL versions
The contiguous v1→v1.0.0→v1.1.0 chain changes version only and retains legacy layout. New canvases use v1.1.0; invalid/unknown/failed migration remains unchanged for explicit repair. Reads preserve YAML/digest/revision; writes create current snapshots.

### Version Identities And Releases
DSL identities use stable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` strings, for example `v1.2.3`.

Do not introduce a schema-only registry entry without its executable migration and fixtures.

### Read Compatibility
Validation selects the exact source schema, applies the explicit upgrade chain, and validates the current shape and cross-object contracts. Returned `document` is canonical current data.

The [canvas contract](#canvas-storage) owns those semantic rules.

Native rendering uses the independently frozen [canvas presentation contract](#display-projection), not the current DSL identity. Every DSL release must verify its explicit mapping to the oldest supported display contract without rewriting source or granting resource authority.

Ordinary edits valid in the original schema continue to upgrade automatically; no historical YAML is rewritten.

## Display projection
Unsupported source remains viewable/exportable without guessed topology; integrity failure forbids export.

### Read And Negotiation
Under `/_redeven_proxy/api/tessiven`, `GET /presentation-contract` returns `formats` and `capabilities`. Unknown well-formed capabilities are ignored rather than treated as authority.

The initial optional `group_layouts` capability enables authored group packing; without it automatic layout preserves the same memberships and relationships.

### Compatibility And Authority
The frozen schema is independent of the DSL registry. Existing display meanings must not change in place.

Resource requests continue to read the original version, check exact bindings and enforce current permissions.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The local Runtime owns the SQLite canvas library and immutable version documents. Canvas references never authorize resource actions; the [Flower and operations contract](../ai/tessiven-runtime-operations.md#flower-document-tools) owns that boundary. Tessiven does not deploy services, discover targets in the background, or synchronize libraries between devices.

### New Snapshots And Failure Boundary
Creation, imports, full save and exact edits write the current DSL. Existing history is never bulk-rewritten.

The [canvas storage contract](#canvas-storage) continues to own atomic startup database upgrades independently.

One normalized snapshot drives graph, object selection, compact summaries, details and Flower references. Native bridges receive display data and revision identity, never historical YAML, credentials or downloaded renderer code.

Removing a supported display format requires an explicit client compatibility-window decision; a DSL release cannot remove it incidentally.

concepts.title: Independent Web Environment Center
concepts.summary: Desktop combines an environment center with its existing local Runtime lifecycle. Web Center has one administrator, with no registration, users, roles, organizations or user ACL service. Labels/hostnames grant no trust. Revisions/sequences fence observations; late completion cannot navigate canceled pending tabs or cancel open route owners.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Shared behavior and host ownership
Shared desktop/src/envcenter owns routes/search/filter/recovery/order/cancellation/Gateway lists. Desktop adapter calls existing lifecycle/windows; Web calls Center HTTP/browser tabs. Shared code imports neither Electron/Node filesystem nor Web auth. Desktop never contacts Center or changes Welcome/navigation/preparation/shutdown. Config/secrets do not sync. cmd/center-contracts generates exact DTO/TS/schema bounds.

Refresh reads authority, not new intent.

## Server entry
Portal, Env and each child use distinct HTTPS origins under one registrable domain/port with matching TLS. Bookmarks are direct. Clipboard denial/absence retains descriptor/manual localized selection; announce success only after actual write.

Center pairs as access-only Gateway after fingerprint confirmation. Runtime independently persists consent through redeven web-binding apply --stdin --yes, binding RuntimeID/origin/clientSPKI/scope/revision. Published Flowersec mutually authenticated TLS1.3 pins signed Runtime service; no inbound app TCP listener.

Operations bind device/route. Browser nonce/exact origins/bounded redemption/single-use code complete handoff; response-loss same-request retry recovers one outcome. Host-only cookies never replace Runtime password/MFA. Logout/security/source/route revocation cancels derived admissions/streams.

## Runtime and child applications
webbinding owns consent, webconnector pinned TLS, environmentcenter admin/directory/proxy. Deployment requires separate stateless Connector via Unix socket with exact peer UID before credentials. Worker holds admitted route credentials only; Center retains admin/factors/master key. Direct adapter is test-only, never deployment fallback.

Control connection owns worker lease; Center loss/logout/revocation closes all streams. Connector restart loses leases; next request requires fresh valid admission. Never replay business HTTP. Systemd/Compose use distinct unprivileged identities; Connector cannot read Center state/TLS keys. IPC preserves bounded permission/capacity/compatibility/offline codes; Runtime payloads cannot invent worker errors. Published controller retries only explicit transient Gateway admission conflicts; invalid/denied/revoked proofs terminate.

Services/editor/graphical viewers use resource origins; trusted proxy retains parent credentials. Editor pins running instance. Graphical access requires scoped Flowersec. Child framing follows authenticated Runtime policy for editor workers; Portal denies framing.

## Plugin application origins
Authenticated parent operations prepare/revoke origins under shared pending/active capacity. Duplicate pending origin is busy; failed/canceled probes release reservation. DELETE fences pending work so late probes cannot revive/replace generations. Each child binds parent route/Runtime admission and cannot call management APIs. Gateway certificates/CONNECT enforce exact namespace/target. Desktop credentials attach only to trusted parent frame.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Center is trusted with plaintext application traffic. This is not browser-to-Runtime encryption against Center. Forwarded headers, loopback, SSH tunnels and browser-supplied headers cannot create management authority.

Web v1 does not implement Desktop SSH/WSL/local preparation, Cloud aggregation or local account/model delegation. Existing Desktop capabilities retain their owners. Remote terminal/files/Git/monitoring/container/Flower and graphical capabilities retain ordinary Runtime permissions and platform conditions.

concepts.title: Web service browser routing and authorization

frontmatter.title: Web service browser routing and authorization

concepts.summary: Registry access mode selects protected unified proxy or Desktop loopback; current Environment/forward authority governs every handoff. Backend normalization accepts `3000`, `:3000` and absolute/scheme-less HTTP(S) with exact `localhost`, numeric `127.0.0.0/8` or `::1`. Renderer checks are feedback only.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Browser sessions
- Browser Local UI unified access uses `/pf/<forward_id>/...`; remote sessions use authorized `pf-<forward_id>` origin and one-time entry. [Loopback access](#desktop-loopback) and [Desktop windows](../desktop/web-service-browser-window.md) own Desktop presentation.
- [Operation progress](managed-service-operation-progress.md) owns per-service feedback. Managed services open through their verified `open-session` result.

## System browser authorization
- Only private-bridge-header admission can mint entries. Memory-only entries cap at 128; remove expired then evict oldest. Loopback HTTP cookies intentionally omit Secure and contain independent random session authority.
- One session per bridge authority/forward expires after 12 hours or shutdown. Memory-only sessions cap at 256 with the same cleanup policy.
- Existing root-mounted forwarding preserves root-relative resources, app-owned `/pf/*`, same-protocol/port redirects, queries, fragments and WebSockets. No new routing rule is added.
- Desktop derives relative paths only from that exact private origin. Local compatibility disables browser handoff and cannot switch mode.

## Desktop loopback
- Persisted `port_forwards.access_mode` alone selects mode. System browsers cannot receive Electron credentials, private `pf-*` substitutions or newly minted unified sessions.
- Bind only `127.0.0.1:0`. Native/placement bridges use canonical numeric-loopback plus exact `/pf/<forward_id>/`; remote routes retain their authorized `pf-*` authority. Keep streaming/oversized replies streaming, not buffered for optional rewriting.
- Each gateway has an independent random credential. [Managed opening](managed-web-service-opening.md) owns explicit reprepare; failed authentication cannot change mode or dial directly.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
[Web Center](web-environment-center.md) opens services/editor on resource-specific sibling origins. Parent Runtime credentials stay in the server; child browsers cannot invoke Env APIs. Editor admission pins its running instance and authenticated Runtime frame policy permits its same-origin worker iframe.

Temporary forwards are memory-only until Save; expired/unknown identities cannot be recreated from request fields. Browser-only Env App retains its popup route; no direct-target fallback or device heuristic changes registry authority.

The cookie admits one proxy origin, never Local UI, Provider/Gateway, Flowersec artifacts or other Desktop credentials. No public fallback, `/pf/<id>` conversion, durable session or alternate proxy is allowed; IPC/startup-report contracts remain unchanged.

Compatibility origin is not direct access, RBI, public listening, Local UI login or application authentication. Random credentials block ambient browser use but do not make loopback a cross-user security boundary.

A closed keyboard disclosure retains technical identity/endpoints/lifecycle/paths; commands and installation steps are never expanded by default.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Collection
Centered header/launcher/toolbar/list. Rows have minimum64px, never fixed height; narrow/localized text wraps. [Layout stability](../ui/page-loading-continuity.md#asynchronous-layout) owns async status.

## Opening restrictions
Unavailable Open retains ordinary icon/native disabled state; focusable wrapper explains why on keyboard/touch/hover. Name actual action/stage. Executable permitted Start becomes primary.

## Review and focus
One drawer presents conclusion, compact resources and actions. Known inventory may replace old inspection; unknown preserves facts. Older/unknown targets retain stop-first and explicit update; originally stopped services remain stopped.

## Templates and versions
Published Floe Tabs own colors, roving focus and labelled panels. Compact source-grouped rows lead to wider deployment/runtime/action details. Dropdown wrappers own the sole focus target/disabled state. Omit redundant available-success copy; retain installed/unavailable reasons. Return from review preserves selection/focus; template changes reset disclosure.

Host/Container/Compose details, install, editing, GitHub import and version review share a fixed desktop action edge: secondary/navigation then right-aligned bounded primary, published large36px buttons. Narrow layouts preserve reading/keyboard order, wrap whole controls, put secondary above full-width primary and use >=44px targets. More matches adjacent outline/radius. Title/categories replace instructions.

Template and installed versions share bounded directory/detail panes: version/state rows, selected trust/source/platform and expandable artifact identity, including current provenance. Narrow panes scroll separately; feedback/submission remain outside the list. Refresh/verification retain selection/focus/scroll/footer. Existing confirmation/stop-first/update authority remains; motion is brief/local or immediate when reduced.

## Installation feedback
Compact form shows service/environment, selected version/change and complete wrapping path/folder action. Avoid duplicate facts, recommendation cards and default explanations. Optional facts/access mode use a closed disclosure summarized by selected mode; published button radios preserve keyboard. Required acknowledgements/advisories/custom-workspace warnings stay outside.

Complete inputs/consent automatically prepare an effect-free local plan. Display resolved directory before single Deploy; no extra manual review/success message. Edits immediately invalidate admission; expiry renews in place without path movement. Inline checking/errors retain footer; failures offer Retry. Close/reopen/identity/permission changes fence stale replies. Deployment needs a fresh click bound to the exact plan. Keep return/close, with narrow Deploy after return on its own row.

Final submission returns immediately to collection with appended accessible status row; admission proceeds independently. Accepted operation supplies validation/environment/deployment progress before inventory. Filters cannot hide it. Status explicitly opens details; completion opens nothing automatically. Rejection offers fresh review; uncertainty looks up the receipt; accepted failures use service recovery. [Progress](managed-service-operation-progress.md#install-admission-and-handoff) owns handoff.

## Execution feedback
One bounded command/output viewport retains earlier reader position. Unknown totals show transferred bytes and indeterminate bar; measured bytes enable speed, fully cached pulls show zero transfer. Layer counts remain separate.

concepts.title: CodeSpace system-browser access
concepts.summary: Desktop resolves trusted resource identity over Environment transport into short-lived loopback entry. The system browser never receives a private Local UI `/cs/<id>` URL, an environment credential, or a raw gateway header. Runtime accepts only this shaped loopback origin or the built-in numeric-loopback origin as presentation metadata; that metadata never selects an upstream dial target.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Resource intent and route ownership
After starting the selected CodeSpace, Env App submits `mode: browser` and its CodeSpace ID through the same root-frame-only IPC used for built-in editor windows.

## One-time entry and browser session
Only main can mint an entry from the gateway object.

Runtime and editor traffic never carries the browser cookie; upstream responses cannot set the reserved cookie name.

An OS-open failure closes the newly acquired gateway and route.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The browser cookie grants only the bound native editor, never Local UI management, a sibling CodeSpace, an environment session, or a Web Service.

## Source and tooling
scripts/dev_desktop.sh freezes HEAD/tracked/nonignored inputs, including authored OKF/builders/embeds, rejects drift and verifies immutable outputs. Generated OKF/ignored assets are outputs. Reuse needs matching source/dependencies/tools/target/settings and intact output; otherwise rebuild, never old bytes. --rebuild forces; REDEVEN_AGENT_FORCE_INSTALL=1 reinstalls three JS packages once. Manifests select managers/locks; redevplugin_build_toolchain.json pins Rust. Capture tool identity without eager install; prepare missing tools only on cache miss. Invalid pins name configuration; drift invalidates preparation.

Resolve physical checkout/parent aliases before ownership/build checks. Managed package-local links may survive aliases, never sibling/external source links. Toolchain CLI uses Node main-module identity. macOS infers static HTTP/HTTPS proxy once only absent any explicit variable (including empty/lowercase) and REDEVEN_DEV_SYSTEM_PROXY=0; preserve NO_PROXY or add loopback. PAC/SOCKS needs explicit policy. Preserve TLS/credentials/integrity; strip inferred proxy only before launch.

Official Node acquisition retries transport/408/429/500/502/503/504 three times with1/2s backoff; permanent HTTP/certificate errors stop. Retain CONNECT/origin/URL/byte diagnostics. Resume owned partials only, freshly check official checksum for cache/download and remove failed bytes. Cargo reuse still stages exact public locked crates and regenerates digest/execution/consumption proof; complete cache allows offline, corruption/compiler error never substitutes. Source changes rebuild whole product, no watch/component shortcut.

## Bundle
Ship Runtime/plugin runtime/standalone Computer Node/released SDK/UI without first-launch downloads; Chromium [install](../ai/computer-use-browser-installation.md) stays explicit. Main pureJS/inlineCSS; frontends build-only, native/updater unchanged. Builder allows main/four preloads/licenses/workers/fonts/Wasm; reject tests/maps/demos/extraASAR and>80MiB including unpacked modules. Report Runtime/Electron separately.

Computer retains released layout/licenses/platform binary, no maps, validates manifest.upstream.json. macOS validates pre-signing/signatures/unsigned Mach-O, normalizing only signature-dependent __LINKEDIT; derive signed record before seal and reject executable/manifest drift. Linux manifest unchanged. Qualify relocated offline helpers without source/globalNode; audit archive/cache/components and distinguish compressed/installed size under equal inputs.

## Build and lifecycle
Desktop/Runtime preparation overlaps; asset-Go/plugin/Computer workers own outputs. Env typecheck/build share checkout lock; Go waits for embeds. Three dependency workers retain serial digest/order. Publish only complete unchanged inputs; cancel/failure stops owned descendants and preserves errors. Dev skips notice freshness, staged/main require it, release runs after assets.

Reuse compatible intact Gateways; drift never auto-upgrades. Repair missing/corrupt owned packages; explicit Update selects build. Dirty bytes enter key; source changes retire generation, missing key creates session cache and owner validates archive. Read-only startup/cleanup uses schema5 connection_id and supported older gateway_id until migration, never trust_profile/changed-record/ledger gatewayID paths. Invalid schema stays unchanged.

Dev gzip1/Brotli4 preserves bytes; release maximizes, profile part of identity. Gateway copies exclude other worktrees/native caches. Record dependency/verification/build timings. Rebuild/reuse acceptance requires saved Gateway, exact Runtime and cleanup, not empty-profile speed. Exit/signals/failure stops only owned services. Electron resolver stdout is path, stderr diagnostics; propagate failure/recheck executable after build.

## macOS identity
Launch profile-owned Redeven Desktop Dev.app through Launch Services; separate signed Redeven Desktop Access Dev.app owns capture/input. Resolve exact fingerprint before stopping/capturing inputs. Explicit access/mac signing identity wins, otherwise unique Apple Development or unique Developer ID Application only if none. Deduplicate keychains; missing/ambiguous/invalid keys fail, no ad-hoc fallback. Stop-only/dry-run needs no keychain.

Certificate+bundleID keeps designated requirement; fingerprint enters cache identity and staging revalidates before resources. Production uses REDEVEN_DESKTOP_MAC_IDENTITY/com.floegence.redeven.desktop-access. Computer manifest inventories helpers/seal, outer Electron signing preserves it. Reject ambiguous/missing app inventory; relay carries only explicit exclusionPID/media metadata.

## Profiles, storage and credentials
Physical checkout owns profile across branches; source changes bundle, not data. Older builds may reject newer state: use compatible Runtime or explicit isolated REDEVEN_STATE_ROOT, never reset/bypass. Before stop/build inspect retired plugin placement without opening platform DBs. Explicit --relocate-storage previews, stops selected profile, applies existing offline journal and verifies; invalid/no-stop fails before shutdown. [Storage](../architecture/storage-ownership.md) owns confined links/relocation. Native acceptance needs public-source runtime, retained state and real sandbox/Worker, not admission fixture.

Unpackaged dev encrypts AES256GCM with retained random0600profile key (no same-user protection); other modes use system storage without constructor probes. Legacy Keychain recovery is explicit, no automatic secrets/preferences read. Atomic migration preserves credentials/Retry/Quit; corruption never resets accounts/Runtime/Keychain.

## Presentation

Use one Current connection card with aligned, selectable, wrapping text/diagnostics/paths/addresses.
- Browser scope, sign-in and certificate tasks share rows, meaningful icons and published outline controls with borders/hover/focus. Preserve specialized QR/recovery-code geometry. Removal drafts cannot look committed; review never shows passwords. Separate footer feedback/actions. Floe owns focus trapping, nested Escape, restoration, variants and forced colors.
- SSH destination fills the adjacent control column in creation/settings. Loading/cached-host failure uses its trailing inset, preserving width/draft/focus; idle indicators take no external column or input clicks.
- Environment inventory uses one published rounded SettingsList with divided full-row actions, platform identity and chevrons. Text, numeric and authentication selectors share both edges and height; switches keep intrinsic size. Authentication uses the published lifetime-gated select to fit long translations. Narrow editors stack without remounting drafts.

## Connection facts
Observations preserve host/container namespaces; failures prove no exit. Explicit Stop clears addresses. Presentation never chooses transport.

- Name the selected Environment before addresses. Never substitute SSH aliases for URL hosts or rely on WSL localhost forwarding. Address count cannot resize settings/move the footer.

concepts.title: Desktop Runtime coordination and readiness
concepts.summary: One target-bound coordinator admits managed Local, WSL, SSH and container lifecycle work. The current binary supplies temporary exact inventory and best-effort stop. Builds, downloads, archive preparation, upload and extraction belong to package progress, never process discovery.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Process lifecycle
### Ownership
Keys combine host authority, exact container engine/id and normalized Runtime root. Native Local keys use the actual canonical state directory, resolving symlinks without equating parent and child. [Scoped Runtime operations](../ai/tessiven-runtime-operations.md#runtime-operations) recheck source/target authority before this coordinator admits a handoff.

### Execution
- Start reuses one verified healthy Runtime. Stop succeeds on empty inventory and verifies termination.
- Restart stops the observed Runtime, starts the installed binary and verifies readiness.
- Update prepares/verifies its package before modification, starts even a previously stopped Runtime and verifies it.
- Refresh observes directly without mutation. Reinstall follows [its recovery contract](desktop-reinstall-operations.md).

Desktop exit/update retires WSL Bridges without stopping WSL Runtime.

### Actions
Direct targets retain lifecycle and Provider Connect/Disconnect actions in every diagnosis. Conflicting actions stay visible but disabled, naming the active operation. Access-only targets offer Open/Connect/refresh-access without lifecycle or management fallback.

## Readiness
### Direct readiness
Native Local Environment is available on macOS/Linux; Windows uses registered WSL Environments. A newly published listener without final status remains pending within the startup deadline. Desktop update warns that Desktop and Local Runtime restart and interrupt Local sessions; Later changes nothing.

WSL, SSH and container observations use the saved channel. Unknown/failed health offers Refresh with its real diagnostic. Pending refresh retains prior diagnosis/startup age but withdraws live Presence; completion replaces it. Main retains credential-free `observed_runtime_control_status` until probe failure or management-configuration change. Gateway failure affects only that route.

A completed probe preserves missing-control diagnostics even when it publishes no Presence. Unknown or unauthenticated status must not become an observed stopped Runtime. Missing diagnostics may guide recovery but never grant live management capability; only current Presence can do so.

Direct lifecycle actions remain available in every diagnosis. Failed nested recovery names the actual operation and retains structured diagnostics; raw stderr appears only in technical details.

### Access and Flower
[Verified access routes](desktop-environment-access.md) owns association/defaults. Gateway directory presence, membership and application probing are distinct; failure never changes routes or starts Runtime recovery.

[Runtime Flower access](../../desktop/src/shared/runtimeFlowerAccess.ts) checks actual protocol/epoch for commands, subscriptions, frames and attachments. Desktop restart does not prove Runtime changed. Welcome admits Flower only with compatible openable Runtime and AI `ready`/`degraded`; transitional states show preparation with a return action, while missing/blocked/unavailable facts cannot admit requests.

## Bridge boundary
- [Process lifecycle](#process-lifecycle) owns coordination and exact-target actions; [readiness](#readiness) owns compatible admission.
- [SSH](desktop-ssh-runtime-operations.md), [WSL](desktop-wsl-runtime-operations.md) and [reinstall](desktop-reinstall-operations.md) define direct execution. [Transport recovery](desktop-transport-recovery.md#transport-recovery) owns bridge generations and disposal.
- [Session/model source](desktop-transport-recovery.md#model-source-sessions) owns target routes, model-process lifetime and session invalidation. Private bridge tokens never move between partitions or attach to public origins.

Runtime owns business services and proxy sessions. User-supplied systemd, Docker or Kubernetes supervision is outside Desktop coordination.

Only Desktop chooses managed Runtime recovery. Optional platform display fields cannot change readiness or compatibility admission.

Runtime control is Desktop coordination, not a general network API or plugin grant. [ReDevPlugin](../architecture/redevplugin-boundary.md) retains its separate execution and capability boundary.

sections.body:
## Authentication and transport
Transport keys bind normalized destination/port/authentication/executable/credential scope. Preserve failure without substitution/replay. macOS/Linux use ControlMaster; Windows uses bounded native OpenSSH plus one child/private Bridge, never WSL/ControlMaster. Cancel owned children only.

No empty retry. Start/Restart/Update retain transient credentials through access/certificate/preparation/verification, never save; observations reject passwords. Probe/inventory/readiness use Connect Timeout, package/startup separate budgets. Windows x64 private-stdout askpass accepts passwords/passphrases, rejects host-key prompts and preserves trust; missing helper fails without secret args/files/logs. Bounded includes omit wildcard/negated picker aliases, not explicit destinations. Persist exact root/container engine+ID apart from label.

## Connection verification and opening
Probes own at most eight reusable HTTP(S) connections and eight concurrent asset requests. Each request defaults to a 10-second deadline including queue time; HTML and all asset batches share a separate 30-second deadline. Caller deadlines and cancellation still apply. Transport failure stops further batches; readiness requires every asset. Always release owned connections; preserve caller-owned Gateway agents. Diagnostics retain observed reasons without credentials. Asset failure does not mean a missing Runtime Service; bridge limits remain unchanged.

Known openable placement remains a dial hint when management observations are stale. Open creates a cancelable operation before bridge/Env App verification. Unknown management state never authorizes Start/Restart. Preflight, retries and readiness share 30 seconds; installation/update retain their lifecycle budget. Bridge establishment allows 15 seconds; failed owned commands escalate TERM to KILL after one second.

Failed bridge/repeated upper stall triggers coalesced5s remote true for exact generation; local -O check proves no peer liveness. Preserve healthy transport; fence failures before retiring owned masters/children. Acquisitions wait for verification/retirement; late reports cannot kill replacements/scopes. Canceling one waiter retains shared verification. Never replay business commands or vary QoS automatically.

## Execution
One operation reuses transport/probes platform once. Only inventory/stop prepares small helper; Start/Stop never build bundles. Update verifies before mutation and exposes acquisition/upload/build. Use public dependencies; install Desktop deps before Env assets.

Parse archives once before writes with256MiB compressed/512MiB expanded bound, including Runtime/Computer/signed plugins. Upload has independent stall deadline; command timeout resumes after final write. Stall/cancel/loss stops owned command; pipe bytes prove no receipt. Password prompts have no upload deadline.

Private Runtime/managed/bin/executables0700, evidence/stamps0600 regardless of umask. Normalization failure preserves live slot; upstream admits executables. Host identity needs confirmed user/root, container exact saved ID. Start/Restart/Update/Reinstall may start container; Stop never does and accepts empty inventory. Signal verified scope only, retain before/after. Wipe may tolerate helper inventory/stop failure only if direct access isolates root.

Remote bounded snippets perform probe/stage/inventory/stop/install/start/verify/isolate/cleanup. Desktop owns order/deadlines/cancel/progress/retry; no target lock/heartbeat/supervisor.

## Progress and results
Use generated signed GitHub installer at selected tag, no Portal duplicate. Existing Launcher measures actual acquisition/transfer; parse complete Downloading Redeven:N% records, stderr diagnostics/stdout stage path. Companion output cannot reset Runtime progress; no extra parser/process/poll.100% proves no activation/readiness. Freeze failure/cancel progress; only activation changes live slot.

Create operation before SSH. Distinguish connection/engine/preparation/command/readiness with technical stderr. Empty success stays pending until deadline; nonzero read=command failure, valid blocked report=Runtime failure, only nonempty malformed=invalid. All lifecycle paths share interpretation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Transport recovery
### Recovery presentation
First load and terminal failures use the full unboxed status surface. After successful admission, recoverable loss uses a compact out-of-flow status with expandable controls/diagnostics; it does not cover the workspace, move content, steal draft focus or expose a full-canvas countdown. Successful protocol and secure-session recovery restores the workspace immediately. Authentication loss and terminal transport failure still withdraw interaction authority.

Local artifact fetch/body acquisition has a 15-second deadline and preserves caller cancellation and upstream retry classification. Paused/failed Desktop state cannot acquire new credentials.

Optional recovery artwork loads separately with fixed placeholder geometry; asset failure cannot hide status or controls.

A 30-second stalled-app timeout shows an actionable failure instead of an endless loading surface.

Each established bridge owns one immutable transport-recovery snapshot with a monotonic `generation` and `revision`, the real `waiting`, `connecting`, `paused`, `ready`, or `failed` phase, completed attempt count, optional SSH transport generation, known retry and recovery timestamps, a structured failure, and explicitly allowed actions.

Lifecycle generation fencing cancels matching Opens so a late response cannot recreate the old session.

## Model-source sessions
- Every `DesktopSessionContextSnapshot` carries `target_route`: Local publishes declared `local_host`/`remote_desktop`; SSH, Gateway and External Local UI publish `remote_desktop`.
- Compaction is a Runtime thread action. Desktop and Env App share canonical timeline/read-state updates rather than inventing transcript messages.
- One Responses transport manager survives control reconnects. Idempotent `ai.thread.transport.release` releases only memory; Floret owns canonical deletion. Exact v4 transport events reject incompatible peers.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Transport recovery IPC is a narrow current-session capability. The separate Desktop Restart handoff exposes only the current window's bounded user-authored state to its fresh session, never ports, tokens, other Environment snapshots, Runtime handles, or launcher operations. Terminal transport failure may preserve the renderer window for diagnosis and navigation, but every previously loaded Runtime surface remains non-interactive until a fresh session is explicitly opened.

Private-origin replacement clears browser storage. Env App includes its saved
plugin composer/comment cache and selected draft route in this same handoff,
flushes the active workspace before capture, and commits restored storage before
acknowledgment. Failed capture or persistence cannot report successful restoration.
Restored cache is user intent only; opening a draft requires fresh server authority.
The draft query and fragment are product navigation, not IPC authority. Restart
admission retains the exact entry origin/path and other query parameters, root
webContents, main frame and document generation while accepting that navigation.

Welcome Flower and Tessiven share compatibility/AI readiness. Returning to preparation disposes stale initialization while parent `ComposerDraftStore` retains drafts. Plugin workers/sandboxes receive no runtime-control endpoint/token; resource access uses released ReDevPlugin brokers and registered adapters.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reverse application streams
After local consent, Runtime redeems its invitation with its own identity and initiates a persistent Flowersec session to the unified public TLS endpoint. Gateway opens a reverse ByteStream on that Runtime's connection and relays both streams with bounded buffers and cancellation.

TLS, WebSocket, streaming responses and secure cookies retain their original semantics.

## Application and management separation
A reverse stream enters the original public Runtime handler. It never acquires a trusted Desktop management marker.

The catalog alone does not authorize service or Runtime process operations.

## Limits and revocation
The shared budget admits at most 32 business connections per member and 1,024 in total, including pending opens. One member exceeding a limit cannot consume another member's allocation.

Other clients and the Runtime attachment stay connected. Reauthorization uses a fresh key, so previous artifacts never regain admission. These effects use published Flowersec session cancellation and relay primitives.

Cloud authorization never closes independent Gateway streams. Local egress cancellation is scoped separately by [Optional Runtime Cloud egress](gateway-cloud-access.md).

## Invitations
Host-issued Runtime invitations require Runtime authentication and explicit consent. Client packages are rdgc1/purpose redeven-gateway-client/version1: one-use secret, exact Gateway ID/key, scoped CA and expiry. Parsers reject cross-purpose use, unknown fields, malformed trust and expiry.

Identical original completion may recover response loss. Desktop/Center retain CA in independent records; display names authenticate nothing. Revocation closes that device's channels without affecting another client/Cloud user.

## Private management
Local/SSH/container adapters verify credentials over the private host socket; public URLs expose device access only. Gateway derives capabilities, never caller-selected/persisted device roles. manage_attachments covers invitations/removal; manage_network covers endpoints/listeners/Host restrictions/egress/reevaluation. Issuance/listing/revocation/receipts require current host proof. Both management capabilities exist together only on that verified request. Removing a Desktop registration preserves remote service/data.

All public device keys are listed/revocable, including host-paired keys. Historical host_managed grants no exemption. Trust schema4 atomically migrates1–3 before readiness, preserving identity/access/revocations; unsupported state stays unchanged.

Private management uses host proof independently of device signatures, but a supplied signature must verify. Signed identity retains requested binding audience for exact connection pinning. Applications/service identity require admitted device keys even over private socket. Self-revocation preserves private management/recovery; refresh cannot pair again. Explicit reauthorization creates a fresh key; challenges/old receipts cannot revive revoked keys.

## Mutation recovery
X-Redeven-Operation-ID binds private mutations. A bounded mode-0600 host-only journal persists intent before effect, response afterward. Same ID/body returns saved result; route/body changes conflict. POST /gateway/v6/operations/query reads the original over the private channel. Retain <=1024 operations/24h. Issuance receipts may contain short-lived packages; never expose journal data in diagnostics/public replies. Expiry grants no replay.

Interrupted effect-before-receipt yields OPERATION_RESULT_UNKNOWN without replay. Desktop stores ID privately and queries after response loss. Confirmed failure clears pending state; unknown/expired stays fenced with inspectable ID. Explicit review acknowledgement clears only the verified Gateway's recovery fence. CLI supports --operation-id and operations query --operation-id, exposing ID on failure. Join/rotation/Cloud route/enrollment keep their domain receipts; refresh cannot authorize/resubmit consent.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Independent enrollment
Runtime owns one Cloud association, owner-issued setup authorization and its existing Flowersec connection controller. Gateway attachment consent cannot authorize Cloud registration. Attachment lookup uses an explicit Gateway identity, or the sole attachment when unambiguous; a selected Cloud route never supplies a default attachment for general lookup or removal. Runtime may select a Gateway route before initial Cloud enrollment, using route/association revision zero; enrollment verifies the actual Cloud target when it becomes known.

A canceled committed operation remains committed.

## Local egress
New Gateways deny egress with an empty destination list. Host administrators configure exact canonical host:port destinations and per-attachment inherit/allow/deny overrides. Wildcards, URLs, paths, duplicate or malformed authorities are rejected. Executable policy uses attachment.admit, access.open and egress.open; no Cloud approval is consulted.

Admission requires the current Runtime attachment certificate, current local policy and unexpired credentials. The published Flowersec HTTPSProxy carries inner HTTPS without exporting Runtime Cloud keys. Public product policy rejects private resolved destinations; the isolated acceptance harness explicitly opts into its private fixture network. No unrestricted proxy or global proxy environment mutation is introduced.

Disabled egress closes only egress reservations. Independent reverse application streams remain available. Removing an attachment closes all streams depending on that attachment. Credential expiry and stale timers cannot restore withdrawn policy. Policy snapshots copy destination lists so callers cannot widen authority by mutating them.

The catalog's effective_egress_allowed is a policy decision, not a reachability result. It combines the active attachment, inherit/allow/deny and the hook decision for the current policy revision. Egress admission requires an active eligible attachment, its current unexpired client certificate and an allowed destination. The authenticated CONNECT request is independent of the reverse application connection: a disconnected reverse channel does not withdraw egress authority, while attachment removal, certificate replacement and policy revocation do. Only a completed route preflight proves the tested destination was reachable at that time. Empty destinations disable forwarding even when policy permission is true.

Reevaluate egress policy uses manage_network, applies only the selected attachment version and committed policy, and runs no application-health or Cloud-registration test. Unsaved editor changes remain drafts. Access.open hooks continue to evaluate individual sessions; this action does not reevaluate that domain.

## No fallback or cross-path revocation
Runtime registration, recovery, Cloud transport and enabled official-platform traffic use the explicitly chosen route. Route failure reports unavailable; it never silently dials Cloud directly. Cloud logout, user removal or binding revocation cannot alter Gateway device trust, attachments or environment passwords/MFA. Cloud sessions remain subject to their own authorization and Runtime security checks.

This explicit acceptance suite stays outside commit, integration and CI gates.

Nonzero/interrupted runs, missing tests/tools/metrics or cleanup failure fail qualification. Preserve the 110 ms/21 commits/s negative regression and profile-exclusion test; no threshold/workload override or waiver.

## Correctness
Fast checks cover indexed records, bounded queues/windows, turn/disclosure identity, keyed disposal, local thinking, structural versus mutable dependencies, sealed bodies and incremental Markdown in Desktop's browser-conditioned Solid/jsdom configuration. Each sequence entry has one mounted owner: classify once, update live fields/first-prose boundaries and dispose removed owners. Read one token snapshot; retained entries must not grow dependencies. Reuse immutable partition/row identities, restored titles and admission-only visibility. Regressions include 2,400-row subscription/identity bounds, 600 retained rows, real browser arrival/DOM placement, plain/reactive cache ownership and user-only prompt history.

Native downward-wheel regressions must shrink offscreen extent during the gesture in both main and child transcripts. Measure every frame and retained paragraph geometry, require the complete input distance without backward movement above 1 CSS px, then verify late-content anchoring after `scrollend`. Unit checks cover both scroll/layout orderings and momentum after the two-frame input expiry. Settled ordinal progress and delayed endpoint samples alone do not certify scrolling continuity.

Per-group observers update changed blockers and dispose removed groups; a 600-group case rejects historical refolding. Body growth cannot advance restoration provenance. Root/child history scans preserve fresh motion. Correct anchors after synchronous completion render and before paint. Every-frame cold-history checks span preview/pending/large-Markdown completion during live generation and native upward wheel input: unintended drift <=1 CSS px, no owner loss, blank frames, duplicate items or malformed cells. Structural batches publish membership once after records are ready; coverage/immutable turn facts add no per-field observers. Cover reconnect, selection, input, approval and terminal state.

The sustained fixture uses real Service, published Floret and fake providers to create 500 canonical turns, 1,000 messages and 1,000 tools and verify all admitted content. No paid provider, user state, raw DB writes or product fallback. Independently produce mixed text/reasoning/Markdown at 80 updates/s, one tool/60 updates, initial 32 KiB body and >=600 seconds in one active turn. Shorter or accelerated fixtures cannot qualify it.

Export canonical terminal outcome/failure before waiting for UI completion; both canonical and observed completion must succeed. Through real history/disclosure controls, compare every generated prose/reasoning item and exact code blocks with canonical content/full Markdown. Reveal parents before children in reading mode, opening only each item's owning sequence; never force hidden clicks or disclosure state. Preserve drafts/focus/selection through drag. Synthetic floating output does not qualify terminal emulation. Responsive timing with a failed terminal fails.

Allow preparation, ten-minute output and complete inspection within the supervised fixture lifetime. A 1,200-row regression forbids geometry reads for preserved/appended baselines and verifies exact interior-gap height after removal. Actual folding protects focus/selection/inspection. Consume published Floret v7.103.1 linear active-path reads and same-read reuse without reconstructing journals or extending completion deadlines.

## History
Published Floret v7.106.1 supplies bounded transaction-local reads, validated ancestry locators and physical body batching. Preserve two-stage navigation, exact membership, budgets and scroll ownership; no new database layout/cache.

Run `scripts/qualify_flower_thread_open.mjs --fixture=<isolated-fixture.json> --output=<evidence.json> --history-scroll-steps=80` with `TestServerFlowerHistoryScrollQualification` for real HTTP decoding and native bidirectional scrolling. A separate `--visual-frames` run captures timestamped compositor JPEGs and section geometry, rejecting visible sections with forced-hidden content. Native automatic skipping must keep newly exposed sections paintable before delayed observers. Inspect frames for flashes, gaps, clipping and overlap. Capture cannot combine with profiling/tracing/opening-time thresholds and is not latency evidence. Retain canceled body/parent-event requests separately from HTTP/sync errors.

`--stability-seconds=1800` (maximum 3600) checks the same visible paragraph/table/code anchor every frame, rejects loading/error/owner-loss frames and compares collected heap plus DOM/document/listener counts. Retain reports. This settled-reading check complements, never replaces, the fixed 600-second/80 Hz active workload.

## Responsiveness
Sample idle/early/late/repeat on the same visible production UI with two PersistentFloatingWindows, >=12 monotonic seconds each. Assert both drafts throughout. Cancellation, release, blur or hidden document invalidates a sample. A nonfocusable Electron host uses the primary work-area origin and pointer isolation before showing, retaining composition, CDP input, DOM focus and interruption checks without native keyboard input.

Read counters before press. One CDP session sends press/move/release with no intervening backend calls. An independent 60 Hz producer cannot await dispatch. Require >=55 offered events/s, >=45 position commits/s and >=80% idle cadence. Budgets remain: drag P95 <=75 ms and work-minus-idle <=25 ms; >=95% prose markers with P95 <=250 ms; frame P95 <=25 ms; reactive P95 <=12 ms/max 50 ms; no main-thread task >=100 ms.

Pair complete MOUSE_DRAGGED async spans by process/identity/scope to compositor presentation; report coalesced/unpresented separately and require >=30 presented/s. Healthy rAF is not input proof. No profiling/screencast during timing or universal/photon claim.
